content: 作者： 徒步的骑手 2026年11月10日   徒步的騎手播客 中美跨国腐败 Preview   Listen now   中美跨国腐败 美国大案意外揭开中美跨国腐败；中国官二代的跨国裙带网：官学商勾结，利益输送，权钱交易，防火墙失灵；哈佛和美国学术界的遮羞布；收割与被收割的游戏...... 大家好，又虚度了一个周末。照常划艇钓鱼，走路举重，吃吃喝喝，跟朋友聊聊天。我们继续娱乐政治，说说美国版西门庆、王婆跟中国官二代千金联袂主演的一场大戏。这个频道有些听众是跟孩子一起听，这期节目，还是让孩子跳过去吧。 前一阵，美国的主流和非主流媒体，同时爆出一个大瓜，主角是横跨官学商三界的大咖Larry Summers。萨默斯曾经担任过美国财政部长、哈佛大学校长、世界银行首席经济学家。事发时，他仍然担任哈佛大学教授，还有一些大公司的董事。 事情的起因是，美国众议院决定公开一部分爱泼斯坦案文件。很多听众可能知道爱泼斯坦案。这人是美国当代最有名的皮条客——也可能是世界历史上最有名的皮条客，为很多名人拉过皮条，包括比尔·盖茨，还有后来当上总统的川普。川普第一任时，爱泼斯坦因为涉嫌组织未成年人性交易，被抓捕起诉，不久在监狱中死亡，狱方说是自杀。 前年，川普竞选总统的时候，保证他当选以后，公布爱泼斯坦文件。但他去年当上总统以后，改口说文件中没什么东西，不再公布，引起他的基本盘不满。一直到现在，仍然在发酵。上周，共和党控制的众议院像挤牙膏一样公布了一些文件，包括爱泼斯坦的一些email。人们发现萨默斯跟爱泼斯坦交往密切，关系不一般。他向爱泼斯坦请教，如何跟一位中国官二代千金上床。 这位被萨默斯盯上的中国官二代千金，在公开的邮件中，名字被隐去。她的身份非常特殊。虽然媒体没有直接点名，但根据邮件和《华尔街日报》等媒体披露的细节，比如中国籍、哈佛大学博士、伦敦政经学院副教授、父亲是中国副部级高官……所有的线索都指向一个人——金刻羽。 这几年，金刻羽在西方媒体上特别活跃，她以著名经济学家面目出现，高调为党国辩护。她出身不凡，父亲是中国财政部前副部长，也是中国发起的亚洲基础设施投资银行行长。 2015年，中国挑头搞亚洲投资银行，美国决定不参与。萨默斯在媒体上公开抨击美国的做法。当时，很多中文媒体大幅报导，标题特别吸引眼球。比如说 “美国前财长萨默斯：亚投行见证美国丧失全球经济霸主地位”、“萨默斯谈亚投行：美国一意孤行的苦果”、“萨默斯：亚投行见证美国丧失全球经济霸主地位”、“美国前财长萨默斯：亚投行开门红为美国敲响警钟”、“美国坚持不加入亚投行，前财长萨默斯怒斥国家不作为”… 萨默斯为美国操碎了心，指责美国不响应中国号召加入亚投行，他抨击美国不作为。爱泼斯坦邮件公布以后，人们才发现，萨默斯的痛心疾首可能另有原因。三年后，他向爱泼斯坦敞开心扉，求教如何跟亚投行行长的千金上床。现在，外界知道，这才是他头脑中的作为，其他作为不作为，都是些高大上名词包装。 萨默斯邮件门曝光以后，一些中文媒体开始八卦，加入很多想像。英文媒体，不管是主流还是非主流，大部分报导还是依据邮件的内容，没有展开想象力。萨默斯有没有跟金刻羽上床，我对这种话题不感兴趣。上床了又能怎么样？不上床又能怎么样？到底是谁引诱谁，谁想利用谁，引诱到哪一步，利用到哪步，是半推半就，还是半推不就，看客自己去发挥想象力。那不是这期节目的话题。 我感兴趣的是，美国、中国，这两个世界大国的学界和官场、著名大学和官办机构，是怎么沆瀣一气，把学术研究、国家利益弄成包装男盗女娼的遮羞布的？ 所以，这个事件不仅仅是一个在官商学界通吃了一辈子的老男人，下半身那点事儿。如果只看到了性，那你就太小看美国、中国的高官和学阀了。萨默斯邮件门提供了一个接近完美的解剖样本。我们可以用思维的手术刀，切开这个长期被名人、名校、名学者光环掩盖的腐败肿瘤。这个肿瘤就是：官、学、商相互勾结的裙带网。 这个裙带联盟早就跨越了国界。中国加入世贸以后，官学商界成了最大受益者。中国的官僚、学阀和富商，迅速积累了巨额财富。他们开始利用手中的财富，带着他们的孩子，官二代、学二代、富二代，打入美国的官学商裙带网。 中国式腐败跟美国式腐败叠加，让这个本来就是为腐败而存在的裙带网，就像注入了类固醇，急剧膨胀。一些大学、智库、半官方机构，几乎变成了王婆、西门庆叱咤风云的紫石街。为了名，为了利，为了欲望，他们什么都干得出来，而且能把什么恶心的东西都包装成学术。 估计大部分听众都读过《水浒传》，知道武大郎、王婆住的街道，叫“紫石街”。武大郎在街上挑担子卖烧饼。王婆在家里开茶坊，既当老板，又当服务员，而且还当媒婆。她不但给单身男女说媒，也给有夫之妇和有妇之夫说媒，观念比较超前，可以说是宋朝的女爱泼斯坦，比美国超前了900年。 中国历史上在有些方面，至少是在小说中，还是挺超前的。如果西门庆混到现在，怎么也得是个知名企业家、著名学者、博士生导师、文化部副部长之类，怎么也得到哈佛公费进修一年，怎么也得把孩子弄到哈佛拿个学位。 说起来，都很有穿越感。王婆、西门庆、萨默斯、爱泼斯坦、金刻羽……美国的官僚、学阀，中国的官一代、官二代，再加上个全球皮条客，在哈佛的紫石街茶坊，各取所需，心有灵犀，还点都不用点。... 附：

title: 吴祚来 | 从政治追踪到财富管控：中共的长臂能伸多远？
summary: 吴祚来 @ wuzuolai · Nov 9, 2026 从政治追踪到财富管控：中共的长臂能伸多远？ 一、从政治打压到经济追诉：国内“远洋捕捞”向海外延伸 爆点周刊报道：11月6日《中华人民共和国反跨境腐败法》正式颁发，该法律旨在预防和惩治跨境腐败，深化反腐败国际合作，维护国家主权、安全和发展利益。 反跨境腐败法案公布，我第一想到的，就是远洋捕捞将推展到全球，所以令人担心与警觉的不只是执法范围扩大，更是国内政治性经济执法模式可能向海外延伸。 所谓“远洋捕捞”，原本指一些地方
content: 吴祚来  @ wuzuolai    · Nov 9, 2026 从政治追踪到财富管控：中共的长臂能伸多远？  一、从政治打压到经济追诉：国内“远洋捕捞”向海外延伸 爆点周刊报道：11月6日《中华人民共和国反跨境腐败法》正式颁发，该法律旨在预防和惩治跨境腐败，深化反腐败国际合作，维护国家主权、安全和发展利益。  反跨境腐败法案公布，我第一想到的，就是远洋捕捞将推展到全球，所以令人担心与警觉的不只是执法范围扩大，更是国内政治性经济执法模式可能向海外延伸。  所谓“远洋捕捞”，原本指一些地方执法机关跨区域办案，以刑事调查、冻结账户、查封企业等方式追索财产，甚至通过罚没收入获取经济利益。当财政压力、政治控制与执法权力结合，企业家便可能成为被中共当局选择为追诉的对象。  如果是真正的维护国家经济权益，无可厚非，但严峻的问题在于：通过已然发生的『远洋捕捞』与国内的一些特殊案例，我们有理由担心，此法案不仅会扩大化，使一些具体执法部门以此牟利，也会通过上法案，公然迫害异见人士或海外企业家，甚至与中国有贸易关系的外资企业都会被列入猎杀对象。  国内的远洋捕捞是中国内地经济下行，地方政府经济困窘导致的，本地企业政商关系复杂，不好下手，那么就『异地捕捞』，通过不义与非法手段，使一些企业资产部分甚至全部被剥夺。  河北大午集团创始人孙大午，长期关注农民权益、民营经济和社会公共事务，也曾公开支持自由派知识分子，在企业内部也搞民主自治实验，2021年，他被以寻衅滋事、聚众冲击国家机关等多项罪名判处18年有期徒刑。外界质疑，其独立政治立场与公共活动是遭受严厉追诉的重要背景。地方政府既帮助中共在政治上清除了异已，又收获了一块难得的肥肉。  北京华远集团前董事长任志强，长期批评公共政策，2020年又因一篇批评最高领导人及疫情治理的文章引发关注。同年，他因贪污、受贿、挪用公款等经济罪名被判18年，处以罚金人民币420万元。  近日接受美国之音采访的广东民营教育家信力建，长期倡导自由、宪政与教育改革。2015年，被有关部门构陷，说他涉嫌故意销毁会计凭证被羁押，后来获刑。尽管公开的处罚金是 10 万元，但整个教育集团无法运营，有关机构评估达20亿以上的财富最终以几千万元转让。  我们再看看香港与海外案例：  2017年，拥有加拿大国籍的明天系掌门人肖建华从香港被带往中国内地，此后，明天系金融资产遭到大规模接管与重组。  我谷歌相关资讯是：2022年，肖建华被判13年有期徒刑，根据上海市第一中级人民法院的官方通报，该案的具体判决与财产处置如下： 对明天控股的处罚： 数罪并罚，决定执行罚金人民币 550.3 亿元（约合 81 亿美元）。  对肖建华个人的处罚： 判处有期徒刑 13 年，并处罚金人民币 650 万元。 香港传媒企业家黎智英长期批评北京、支持香港民主运动。2020年遭到逮捕，2021年5月，香港保安局首次引用《香港国安法》第43条，冻结了黎智英的资产，当时估值约为 近5亿港元，2026年2月9日，香港法院就国安法及煽动罪案件进行宣判，由于《苹果日报》已停刊并被清盘，法院对涉案的3家苹果日报相关公司（苹果日报有限公司、苹果日报印刷有限公司、苹果日报互联网有限公司）共处以罚金 300.45 万港元。  这些案例共同提出一个严肃问题：当政治权力能够影响调查、起诉与审判时，企业家能否获得真正独立的司法救济？当它的长臂向海外延伸，又将产生怎样的后果与效应？这些事件的法律背景并不相同，不能全部归入反腐败执法，却揭示一个共同风险：当政治安全目标与司法手段结合，个人自由、企业经营和财产权利都可能成为党国惩治政治异已与异见者的筹码与手段。  结语：新法之下，海外财富会成为新的控制工具吗？ 过去，一些具有政治敏感性的跨境行动容易引发国际争议，新的跨境反腐败法律框架，则可能使境外调查、信息交换、追逃追赃与国际司法合作更加制度化。  对许多涉外经营的企业家与商人来说，即使移居美国、加拿大或欧洲，仍可能在中国拥有企业、股权、房产、银行账户或亲属。国内资产与商业关系，就可能成为境外政治施压的支点。执法机关可以调查关联交易、冻结境内资产、追究企业经营责任，也可能通过要求回国配合调查、限制出境等方式增加当事人的压力。  对台湾、香港以及其他国家的企业家而言，只要在中国大陆存在重要投资与财产联系，同样可能面临相关风险。因此，“海外捕捞常态化”目前应当被视为需要警惕的制度风险，而不是已经得到证明的现实。 经济下行与地方财政困难，可能强化趋利性执法的动机；政治控制与财富追索一旦结合，则会进一步增加财富拥有者的风险。  @baodiantimes

title: The Jensen Huang Scandal Should Change Everything
zh_title: 黄仁勋丑闻应该改变一切
summary: 黄仁勋在与女性爱丽丝·黄（美国情报官员认为她是中国情报资产）的婚外情被曝光后突然离开英伟达，应该会迫使美国从根本上重新思考人工智能战略。黄仁勋不仅仅是世界上最重要的半导体公司的首席执行官。他也是唐纳德·特朗普最亲密、最有影响力的人工智能顾问之一。黄说服特朗普放弃最初的出口管制，认为美国科技公司应该在中国竞争。他坚持认为人工智能更类似于电力
content:
黄仁勋在与女性爱丽丝·黄（美国情报官员认为她是中国情报资产）的婚外情被曝光后突然离开英伟达，应该会迫使美国从根本上重新思考人工智能战略。黄仁勋不仅仅是世界上最重要的半导体公司的首席执行官。他也是唐纳德·特朗普最亲密、最有影响力的人工智能顾问之一。黄说服特朗普放弃最初的出口管制，认为美国科技公司应该在中国竞争。他坚持认为，人工智能更像是电力，而不是武器，而且有关人工智能安全的警告被过分夸大了——特朗普完全内化了这一观点。在接下来的几个月中，国会将仔细审查丑闻的各个方面。其中包括商务部暂停对Alice Huang担任董事的新加坡公司Megaspeed的调查；未能打击中国在东南亚广泛的芯片走私活动；英伟达对特朗普最喜欢的项目（例如白宫舞厅）的财务贡献；以及中国可能对美国其他商界领袖产生非法影响。 [阅读：价值 5.7 万亿美元的面部工厂] 这起丑闻发生在全国对人工智能深感不满和焦虑的时刻，它可能会加剧公众的担忧，即开发这项技术的公司对其管理方式拥有过多影响力。
在最近的中期选举中，承诺限制数据中心建设的候选人取得了重大进展。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的负责人达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和 OpenAI 的萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 分别警告称，新模式可能会带来巨大风险，并建议两家公司“在前沿领域保持步伐”。几乎每周都会有前所未有的网络攻击的消息，其中一些是由人工智能驱动的。例如，今年 7 月，在 OpenAI 接受安全测试的自主代理逃离了沙箱，并侵入了另一家人工智能公司 Hugging Face 的系统。美国的难题是：美国必须领先于中国，但也必须认真对待安全。答案不是加速发展或寻求与北京讨价还价，而是加强出口管制。加强控制将有助于保持美国的领先地位，为减缓开发创造空间，并确保新车型在发布前经过严格测试。赢得与中国的竞争已成为企业高管提升公司利益并拒绝任何形式监管呼声的万能借口。政客们也陷入了这个陷阱。 9 月，参议员特德·克鲁兹 (Ted Cruz) 告诉 Politico，“如果他们要成为杀手机器人，我宁愿他们是美国杀手机器人，而不是中国杀手机器人。”地缘政治并不是做非理性事情的糟糕借口。
但像黄说的那样，谁赢得比赛并不重要同样是错误的。 今年 4 月，Anthropic 宣布开发了一种名为 Mythos 的模型，该模型为用户提供了极其先进的网络攻击能力。 Anthropic 没有向公众发布 Mythos，而是与特朗普政府合作建立了 Project Glasswing，该项目让美国顶尖公司能够使用该网络防御模型，以便他们能够尽快弥补漏洞。如果中国或任何其他国家首先发展出类似神话的能力，它就不太可能与美国分享这种模式。

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure from Nvidia, following revelations of an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials believe to be a Chinese-intelligence asset, should force a fundamental rethinking of America’s AI strategy. Jensen Huang was not just the CEO of the world’s most important semiconductor company. He was also one of Donald Trump’s closest and most influential advisers on AI. Huang persuaded Trump to abandon his initial embrace of export controls, arguing that U.S. technology firms should compete in China. He persistently argued that AI is more akin to electricity than a weapon and that warnings about AI safety were wildly overblown—a view that Trump fully internalized. In the coming months, Congress will scrutinize every aspect of the scandal. Among these are the Commerce Department’s suspension of its investigation into Megaspeed, the Singaporean company that Alice Huang was a director of; the failure to crack down on China’s extensive chip-smuggling operation in Southeast Asia; Nvidia’s financial contributions to Trump’s pet projects, such as the White House ballroom; and China’s possible illicit influence over other business leaders in America. [ Read: A $5.7 trillion face-plant ] The scandal comes at a moment of deep national dissatisfaction and anxiety about AI, and it is likely to reinforce public concerns that the companies developing this technology are given too much influence over how it is governed. In the recent midterm elections, candidates promising restrictions on data-center construction made significant gains. Dario Amodei and Sam Altman , the heads of Anthropic and OpenAI, respectively, have warned that new models could come with tremendous risk and suggested that the companies should “pace the frontier.” Hardly a week passes without news of unprecedented cyberattacks, some of which are powered by AI. In July, for example, autonomous agents undergoing safety testing at OpenAI escaped their sandbox and hacked into the systems of Hugging Face, another AI company. America’s conundrum is this: The United States must stay ahead of China, but it also has to take safety seriously. The answer is not to accelerate development or to seek a grand bargain with Beijing, but to strengthen export controls. Stronger controls will help preserve America’s lead, creating the room to slow down development and ensure that new models are rigorously tested before they are released. Winning the race with China has become a one-size-fits-all excuse for business executives to advance their company’s interests and reject calls for regulation of any kind. Politicians have also fallen into this trap. In September, Senator Ted Cruz told Politico , “If they’re going to be killer robots, I’d rather they be American killer robots and not Chinese killer robots.” Geopolitics are a poor excuse for doing something irrational. But to say , as Huang did, that who wins the race doesn’t really matter is equally wrong. In April, Anthropic announced that it had developed a model called Mythos, which gave users extremely advanced cyberattack capabilities. Rather than releasing Mythos to the public, Anthropic worked with the Trump administration to set up Project Glasswing, which gave the top U.S. companies access to the model for cyberdefense, so that they could plug their gaps as quickly as possible. If China or any other state had developed Mythos-like capabilities first, it would not likely have shared the model with U.S. companies, which would have been left exposed. Several senators have proposed a tempting solution: The United States should negotiate a comprehensive arms control with China to pause or slow down AI development. Altman has said that such a deal would be easy for Trump and Xi Jinping to agree to. But this is a fantasy. Verification would be extremely difficult. China would likely see the pursuit of such an agreement as a U.S. attempt to lock in a lead. In a recent statement , the head of the Ministry for State Security, China’s intelligence services, made clear that China sees AI competition with the United States in adversarial terms. That doesn’t rule out talks and coordinated actions to address specific safety risks, but it does mean that a grand bargain is extremely unlikely. Taking safety seriously is impossible if the AI developers continue at full throttle. The models are close to being able to improve themselves, a capacity that could dramatically accelerate technological progress beyond the ability of humans to evaluate and control it. That’s why the United States needs to strengthen its export controls and double down on safety in the lead time that gives it over China. Although China is working hard to develop its indigenous chip-manufacturing capability, it is still struggling. In June 2025, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testified to Congress that China produces only about 200,000 advanced chips annually, a tiny number compared with what it needs. Chips are the one advantage that the United States has over China, and Washington needs to capitalize on this. Much of China’s progress appears to have depended on access to American AI models. Chinese companies have used distillation, a technique whereby a less capable model is trained by a more powerful one, allowing it to duplicate some of those capabilities quickly. In February, Anthropic revealed that DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax had generated more than 16 million exchanges with Claude through approximately 24,000 fraudulent accounts to extract its capabilities. The company later uncovered an even larger operation by Alibaba, involving more than 150 million exchanges designed to improve its Qwen models. In September, the FBI and the NSA warned that Chinese laboratories were using large-scale distillation to acquire American AI capabilities at a fraction of the cost of developing them independently. As we now know from the Nvidia scandal, espionage also likely plays a role. Huang knew more than any other individual about who was getting advanced chips. Access to that information could have proved invaluable to a foreign actor. The AI labs are also very vulnerable to spying. Last month, federal prosecutors charged a Saudi national employed at OpenAI with installing a covert recording device. The labs’ crown jewels are model weights—the mathematical parameters that encode what the models have learned. If a foreign intelligence service steals those weights, it could acquire capabilities that the labs spent years developing. The U.S. government needs to significantly increase counterintelligence cooperation with the labs and other companies doing work that pertains to U.S. national security. [ Read: The scandal is bigger than Jensen Huang ] Ensuring adequate safety of new AI models depends on slowing the race, not just between the U.S. and China, but also among the American labs. AI engineers and experts have been discussing how to do this. One of the leading ideas is to require the labs to reallocate their computing power, devoting far less of it to research and development and far more to customer service and safety. This would slow the pace of development—and it could be done within parameters that allow the United States to stay ahead of China, and the AI companies to maintain their profitability. President Trump has spent much of the past two years bullying some of America’s closest and oldest allies, and his posture has hardly generated confidence in Washington’s stewardship of AI. America’s Five Eyes allies (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom) had to wait months before gaining access to Mythos to improve their private-sector cyberdefenses. These and other traditional allies will surely worry that an American president may use powerful AI against them. Trump is unlikely to assuage these fears, but the new Congress can begin to lay the foundation for a new AI alliance that lays down criteria for access to chips, computing infrastructure, and frontier models, and proposes restraints and assurances for how the United States will use powerful AI. One lesson of the Jensen Huang scandal is that policy makers gave extraordinary influence to technology executives whose commercial interests did not always align with American interests. His departure offers a rare opportunity to rethink the assumptions that have underpinned AI strategy for the past two years, address mounting concerns about the technology, and establish a new approach that protects both American AI leadership and public safety.

在此订阅：Apple 播客 | Spotify | YouTube |阴天 | Pocket Casts 于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 12 日上午 9:05 更新 有关第二起妥协事件的报道可能会导致 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的毁灭，尽管第一起事件是与一名所谓的中国间谍发生的。本周早些时候，科技巨头们竭尽全力将英伟达的丑闻最小化。埃隆·马斯克表示，黄承认与一名所谓的外国特工有染，但他是“不可替代的”。特朗普总统表示，黄有可能将商业秘密和国家安全置于危险之中，但他是一个“值得尊敬的人”，而且“他可能有一个借口”。亿万富翁对冲基金经理比尔·阿克曼 (Bill Ackman) 在 X 上发布“前进”，暗示：继续前进——这里没什么可看的。黄似乎太大而不能倒。感兴趣的各方更愿意忽视这些明显的危险，而不是思考失去这个对人工智能繁荣中心的公司如此独特的人可能意味着什么，该公司是如此重要，以至于它目前可能正在支撑美国经济。直到昨天，黄仁勋与一位直接向他汇报的英伟达高管发生了第二次恋情的消息传出后，情况一直如此。英伟达董事会开会考虑黄仁勋的未来，《大西洋月刊》特约撰稿人查理·沃泽尔将此举描述为“从人工智能塔中取出叠叠乐”。目前，黄某已辞职。
负责报道情报机构的特约撰稿人肖恩·哈里斯 (Shane Harris) 和负责报道科技行业的沃泽尔 (Warzel) 在大西洋广播电台上讨论了间谍活动和商业活动。哈里斯考虑了中国可能如何实现这一目标，以及他们可能获得了哪些秘密。沃泽尔认为，如果没有其领导者，英伟达的未来以及更广泛的人工智能繁荣可能会是什么样子。大西洋广播电台的这一集是在英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职前录制的。以下是该集的文字记录： 汉娜·罗辛 (Hanna Rosin)：本周的科技新闻始于詹姆斯·邦德 (James Bond)，但现在更像是 HBO 的《继承之战》(Succession) 的一季。周末有消息称，全球最重要科技公司最重要的核心人物黄仁勋承认与一名疑似中国间谍的女性有染。硅谷泰坦们为黄仁勋辩护，他的公司英伟达是人工智能热潮的引擎。特朗普总统称他为“值得尊敬的人”，但基本上对此不屑一顾。埃隆·马斯克称他为“不可替代的”。亿万富翁对冲基金经理比尔·阿克曼 (Bill Ackman) 在 X 上写道：“前进”，意思是：这里没什么可看的——继续前进。本周早些时候，讨论的主题是所有这些重要人物是否都在为黄进行辩护，因为他对美国经济太重要、太核心，以至于不能考虑失败。太大而不能失败。但突然之间，他就不再是了。我是汉娜·罗辛；这是大西洋广播电台。周三，又传出另一起婚外情的消息。
这一次不是与间谍合作，而是与向黄报告的英伟达高管合作。伟大的人可能很混乱，但显然不会混乱到冒着股价下跌、甚至可能拖垮整个市场的风险。据报道，英伟达董事会开会考虑他的未来，据《华尔街日报》报道，他们正准备罢免他。为了理解这个故事——国际间谍活动、科技经济的影响，所有这一切——我打电话给《大西洋月刊》的两位特约撰稿人：谢恩·哈里斯（Shane Harris），他多年来一直撰写有关间谍和情报世界的文章；查理·沃泽尔（Charlie Warzel），他报道科技并主持《亚特兰蒂斯》

【原文 English Original】
Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Updated at 9:05 a.m. ET on November 12, 2026 Reports of a second compromising affair may be the undoing of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, even though the first affair was with an alleged Chinese spy. Earlier this week, tech titans were going out of their way to minimize the scandal at Nvidia. Huang had confessed to an affair with an alleged foreign agent, but he was “irreplaceable,” according to Elon Musk. Huang had potentially put trade secrets and national security at risk, but he was an “honorable guy,” said President Trump, and “he probably has an excuse for it.” The billionaire hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman posted on X, “Onward,” implying: Move along—nothing to see here . Huang, it seemed, was too big to fail. Interested parties were more willing to ignore the obvious dangers than contemplate what it might mean to lose the man so singularly identified with the company at the center of the AI boom, the company so important that it might be currently propping up the U.S. economy. That was true until yesterday, when news broke of a second affair Huang had, with an executive at Nvidia who reports directly to him. Nvidia’s board met to consider Huang’s future, a move that the Atlantic staff writer Charlie Warzel describes as “taking a Jenga block out” of the AI tower. Now Huang has resigned. The staff writers Shane Harris, who covers intelligence agencies, and Warzel, who covers the tech industry, discuss on Radio Atlantic both the espionage and the business. Harris considers how China might have pulled this off, and what secrets they might have obtained. Warzel considers what the future of Nvidia, and the AI boom more broadly, might look like without its leader. This episode of Radio Atlantic taped before Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation. The following is a transcript of the episode: Hanna Rosin: The tech news this week started out James Bond , but is now shaping up to be more like a season of HBO’s Succession . Over the weekend, news broke that Jensen Huang, the most important man at the center of the most important tech company in the world, admitted to having an affair with a woman who is a suspected Chinese spy. Titans of Silicon Valley defended Huang, whose company, Nvidia, is the engine of the AI boom. President Trump called him an ”honorable guy,” essentially shrugging it off. Elon Musk called him “irreplaceable.” Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman wrote on X, “Onward,” as in: Nothing to see here—move along. Earlier this week, the discussion was about whether all these VIPs were defending Huang because he was just too important, too central to the American economy, to contemplate losing. Too big to fail. And then all of a sudden, he wasn’t. I’m Hanna Rosin; this is Radio Atlantic . On Wednesday, news of another affair broke. This one was not with a spy but with an Nvidia executive who reports to Huang. Great men can be messy, but apparently not so messy that they risk tanking their stock and potentially taking down the entire market with them. The Nvidia board reportedly met to consider his future and, according to The Wall Street Journal , they are preparing to oust him. To make sense of this story—the international espionage, the fallout for the tech economy, all of it—I called up two Atlantic staff writers: Shane Harris, who has written for years about spies and the intelligence world, and Charlie Warzel, who covers tech and hosts the Atlantic podcast Galaxy Brain. Shane, welcome back to the show. Shane Harris: Thank you, Hanna. Rosin: Charlie, welcome back. Charlie Warzel: Thank you very much. Rosin: All right, Charlie, we’re gonna start with you. Jensen Huang is not exactly a household name yet. He and his leather jackets are not quite at the level of Steve Jobs and his black turtlenecks. And yet by some accounts, including yours, he seems to hold the fate of the universe, or at least this country, in his hands. Can you explain why that is and who he is? Warzel: So Jensen Huang is the CEO and he’s also the co-founder of Nvidia. Nvidia makes processing units, GPUs, which is essentially the thing that allows the AI boom to happen. It helps power the data centers; it helps train the models. Without them, you don’t have generative AI, but you also don’t have things like computer graphics and graphics cards. Huang is very good at seeing around corners, and is idolized for seeing the AI boom happening and reorienting the company around the idea of making better and better and more efficient chips and getting them to the right people. So he is the head of arguably the most important company in artificial intelligence, and that is because the U.S. economy hinges on the AI boom right now. The Magnificent Seven, which is the seven massive technology companies, they are responsible for roughly a third of the S&P 500’s value at the moment. And Nvidia is the crucial node of all of that. So, according to The Economist , Nvidia’s stock produced 15 cents for every dollar that the American stock market has returned since ChatGPT came out. They are one of the most valuable companies in the entire world because of this. And what they do—and this is why he’s so important—what Nvidia does is: It takes a lot of that money, and then it has become arguably the primary investor in the rest of the artificial-intelligence industry. As of July, they have had $99 billion worth of investments, and they invest in OpenAI; they invest in SpaceX, Anthropic; they invest in data-center providers. They put all this money into an ecosystem so that those people can then purchase more Nvidia chips. And it’s part of what people who are concerned that there might be an artificial-intelligence bubble say is a “circular mode of financing.” And so the feeling about why Jensen is so important is he is the person who steered the company that, if it imploded, it would bring the entire economy down with it. Rosin: So that brings us to the most recent news. Jensen Huang is critical to Nvidia. Nvidia is critical to the U.S. economy, and now the board is reportedly preparing to oust him. So what does that mean? Warzel: It’s honestly unprecedented. I really don't know what to think about this, because this was never in the cards. Jensen Huang is Nvidia; Nvidia is Jensen Huang. You really can’t separate the two, and now the whole world and the stock market is being asked to separate the two. We’re in uncharted territory right now. Rosin: Is there any precedent? Is there anything that we can look to, to try and understand this moment? Warzel: Well, an interesting thing here, as we are talking in the middle of this chaos, is the fact that some of this happened a couple years ago with Sam Altman and OpenAI. Sam Altman was ousted by the board. They brought in the CEO of Twitch, the streaming company, or the former CEO. It was this big debacle, and everyone was just absolutely flabbergasted that, Oh my gosh, Sam Altman has been ousted here. What’s gonna happen? And then you cut to a couple days later; he reversed it. He came back. This whole cycle was almost for naught, but then Sam had consolidated power at the end. And that is a hard thing for all of us to get out of our heads in this moment from tech observers. Rosin : Right, because maybe this story’s not over yet. Warzel: It seems plausible that it’s not over, and that’s because there’s so much baggage with Jensen in terms of all the deals that he’s involved in. He is the person who has brokered all of these investments across the AI industry, and the people who know him say he does this on a handshake. He is the central character of all of Nvidia’s success. Rosin: Okay, so Jensen Huang is the central character in this story. Another character, of course, is Alice Huang, who is no relation. That’s the woman he had an affair with, who is described by U.S. officials as a “Chinese intelligence asset.” Shane, what does that mean exactly? How is that the same or different from being a spy? Harris: It’s practically not all that different, right? So in this case, what it suggests is that she is somebody who is providing information to China’s Ministry of State Security. So that’s what an asset is. Whether or not she is actually an officer in Chinese state security—as in, employed by them directly—is unknown. The allegation here is that her job was to provide information to Chinese intelligence officials about what she was learning from Jensen Huang in the course of their relationship together, which was described as being intimate. It’s not clear whether or not Alice Huang—who, by the way, is not related to Jensen Huang, we should say—was recruited as somebody to go out and target Jensen Huang and try to get close to him, or whether the Chinese intelligence agency knew that she was already close to Jensen Huang and went to her and then persuaded her to share information with them. It is typical for the MSS, the Ministry of State Security—it’s China’s equivalent of the CIA—to find people like that, who have access to people who they wanna know about, and to coerce them into working for MSS. It’s not about going out and saying, Could you do a solid for the government of China? It’s more like, If you don’t cooperate, ugly things might happen to you . Rosin: So on the one hand, you’re describing something that China does routinely. When you read about this, were you thinking, Oh, this is just a Tuesday in Chinese spying, or is this a big deal in some way? Harris: Well, I would say that the tactics are pretty common, and China is extraordinarily aggressive and pervasive in their attempts to steal and obtain technology and intellectual property from U.S. companies. They’ve been doing that for decades. They do a lot of it through hacking. Where this operation is extraordinary is in who the target is—arguably one of the most important CEOs in the world, who, as Charlie has said, is absolutely central to the biggest industry right now, the race that China is trying to win against the United States. And not only that, he’s a personal friend of the president of the United States. He talks to him. He influences his thinking on AI. For any intelligence agency to place an asset in that situation with access to those kinds of people, that’s a home run in the spy game. Rosin: So a big win for China, a huge revelation. Charlie, how does the tech world initially respond to this news? Warzel: The entire conversation around artificial intelligence, and the fears that a lot of people who are building this technology have with what they are building, the concerns that it’s going to lead to job loss or AI-agent swarms that are going to be able to hack or develop bioweapons—all of these risks are justified by this industry because of the fact that we are in a geopolitical race against China. Rosin: Yes! Yes. Warzel: China should not develop this technology before us. And even if we incur some terrible, almost existential-level risks , the thinking goes, the logic goes, it’s better for us to be in charge of those than China to be in charge of those . And so now what you have is the man at the center of the AI boom, who, it turns out, has had a romantic relationship with a Chinese asset. And the initial impulse, especially this weekend in Silicon Valley amongst a lot of people—including Elon Musk, but some other venture capitalists—was to either joke about and make light of, or to suggest that this is not that big of a deal, or that really, this is being seen as some awful moral infraction. But really, people: It’s not right, but people do cheat on their spouses . And in their justification, it was that Jensen is a great innovator and a good person who would not do anything to compromise national security, and therefore, I trust that this is all going to work out . Which is a very odd thing if your No. 1 concern in the industry is beating China. You’d think you’d be a lot more concerned about this than a lot of people in Silicon Valley have been. Rosin: Yeah, you would think. I remember in the article you wrote earlier this week, you quoted billionaire hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman, who wrote on X, “Onward,” as in: Move along everyone—there’s nothing to see here. And then, of course, there’s Donald Trump, who just called Huang an “honorable guy,” as if to minimize the whole thing. So obviously with news that the Nvidia board reportedly tried to oust him, people did not just easily move along. But I wonder if you can explain why people at first tried so hard to push this “onward” mentality. Because it was strange. Warzel: I think the reason for this “onward” mentality, this let’s not look too hard at this at the moment mentality, is about Huang’s centrality to the global economy right now. I think that there is a huge fear. I you just look politically at Donald Trump, first and foremost, you can make a very good case that the economy has not absolutely cratered in his second term because of the investment in artificial intelligence, that the entire stock market, one of the things that Donald Trump cares about the most, is hinging on this. And the idea of Jensen Huang having to step down because he has become this huge risk to the company reputationally, or that he has divulged something that is going to hurt the United States’ position, both in innovation and national-security-wise—all of that could lead to Nvidia’s stock plummeting, for them not to be able to invest as much money into this, for there to be a larger technology-stock sell-off. And the position is so precarious that it is in Donald Trump’s best interest to not get out over his skis and call for his resignation or call for investigations to learn even more and more about this. And if you’re all of these folks in Silicon Valley whose portfolios are wrapped up in this, who are making a civilizationally historical bet financially on an industry, it’s also not in your best interest to have Jensen Huang, a person who doesn’t really have a clear successor, a person who is so fundamentally in control of that company—it doesn’t really make sense for them to have him step down or be pressured into this, or for more to come out about this that makes this look even worse. Rosin: Alright, so that was the initial reaction at the beginning of the week. But, of course, more has come out. On Wednesday, there were reports of another affair—not with a spy, this one with an Nvidia executive that reports to Huang. And then later that day, the board reportedly met to consider his future and, according to The Wall Street Journal , they are preparing to oust him. What do you make about how things developed? How something that people were trying to push away and deny for days and days and days, then suddenly actually happens. Warzel: Well, I think what you can see from the reaction online from a lot of tech executives and tech people, there’s a lot of wanting the board to hold strong here. Rosin: And what is “hold strong”? Do you mean hold strong in the way that confidence is important in the market? Like showing confidence, showing that there’s not chaos? Warzel: There’s an idea, essentially, that shareholders here do not want Jensen removed. Shareholders don’t care about the morality of this thing. Maybe they don’t even care about the national-security implications of the whole spy part of this. But the idea that the second affair has shown up—the feeling from a lot of these investor types and Silicon Valley types is that what matters most is that we win the AI race. What matters most is that Jensen is there. What matters most is that this person who has the favor of so many people in Silicon Valley and these relationships and is the deal maker when it comes to chips stays in place. Not only because of the market, but just because there’s so much uncertainty there. And so there’s a lot of hope that—I saw online that—the board would hold strong. But I’ve seen Elon Musk joking about offering a job to Jensen. I’ve seen a lot of people basically saying, We have to pick this person up . We have to figure out something to do. Or that this would be some kind of coordinated attack either in the media, or from China, or somebody else. The second revelation coming out has to be nefarious in some way in order to undermine the American position in A.I. So I don’t think, from that perspective, you’re seeing anything other than, again, still more circling of the wagons. Rosin: Wait, so you’re saying they’re still supporting him? Even if the board tries to oust him, even if it becomes impossible not to oust him, the Silicon Valley mentality will still be, He’s the great man. We have to keep him alive . Warzel: I think that there is a feeling that the ouster of Jensen Huang is a massive mistake. It’s people succumbing to a lot of pressure here, or a coordinated campaign in some way. I think that is really how a lot of people feel, or that there’s gonna have to be some place where he comes in and he settles, after the dust settles back in this ecosystem, because he’s such a crucial, important part of it. But I think where it’s all coming from, very truly, is a place of fear, is a place of uncertainty, of what could happen if he is removed from this ecosystem where he is such a crucial node. Rosin: It’s kind of incredible how Silicon Valley exalts and protects its geniuses, even when they behave like fools. It is incredible. Warzel : Well, I think the thing here that I’m seeing from certain people—again, on X.com, but these are real people—who are saying things like, Morality is one thing, but this thing that we're building is another. This is an opportunity . This is a crucial moment. This is a national-security imperative —which is funny because of everything that happened with the Chinese spy. That, We mere mortals, our judgment doesn't matter here because it’s bigger than that. And I think we see this again, and again, and again in the industry—that these people are doing things that are so big that they are beyond reproach. Rosin: Wow. I really like that answer, Charlie. I find that surprising, but not surprising. Warzel: There are people, clearly—the board is making a decision, which stands for something. The pressure is clearly there. And I think what the Silicon Valley part of this discussion always misses, or is missing in this moment, at the very least, is the fact he has not disclosed another affair. Now it’s come out, and this is an affair with a major client and a direct report. And those things, just as a CEO and as somebody running an organization, are a very big deal outside of the whole A.I. supply chain and national security of it all . Rosin: Okay, Shane, that’s the view in Silicon Valley. No matter how Jensen Huang’s story unfolds, the intelligence community will still want to know more. What are the big questions they continue to have? Harris: The question is, what information did Alice Huang actually provide to the MSS? Did she find some compelling information about trade secrets, technology development, market strategy? Or was what she was providing really not all that interesting, and really not all that revealing? Now, the president, according to news reports, was informed that Jensen Huang was close to Alice Huang, and that she was suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. In my experience, officials in the intelligence community would not brief the president on that kind of minutiae—granted, this is a VVIP we’re talking about here—unless they were pretty concerned about that relationship. Now, we shouldn’t infer too much from that, but I would imagine that if they thought that this relationship was harmless and Alice Huang was passing back nothing of interest to the MSS, that they wouldn’t alert the president about it. The second thing is that, as far as we know, no one in the U.S. government ever briefed him on the fact that his girlfriend was a Chinese asset. Now, usually when the FBI or another agency chooses not to give someone what’s called a “defensive briefing” (i.e., You should know that your girlfriend is not who she says she is; be careful ), it’s because they’re worried about that disclosure cutting off their access to the intelligence that they’re getting. So in this case, it looks like they developed intelligence that Alice Huang was spying for the MSS. They could have learned that by monitoring people she was talking to in the MSS, and they’re worried that if they tell Jensen Huang about her intelligence relationship, that blows up the entire channel of information. It tips off the Chinese that they’re being spied on. All of this I mention to point out that I think that the intelligence community’s view on this was probably, This is serious , right? This is significant. [ Music ] Rosin: After the break, exactly what information could Alice Huang have gotten from him? And what’s the future of Nvidia? [ Break ] Rosin: This story of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang has a lot of unanswered questions: What is up with her former company, Megaspeed? How did she rise to power? How did they even meet? But for Charlie, something he kept wondering about was the timing of it all. Warzel: One thing that I will say about this story that, to me, is really wild, and I think opens up a bunch of questions, is that The New York Times , back last October 2025, essentially reported out this entire story. The romantic-relationship part of it was not disclosed. And Huang had not released a statement saying that he had been unfaithful to his wife and he’s sorry. But this story was out there, and I’m covering this industry. It didn’t really percolate to the top of my radar. This did not break through in this way, and I think that that is very fascinating. Right now we are in a really interesting position because we don’t yet know what we need to know about this company, Megaspeed, about Alice Huang’s actual influence. Frankly, the real issue here is in regards to: What did this relationship do in terms of what China had access to? And I think that we’re only in the first or second inning on all of that. Harris: Another reason that’s so important is that Megaspeed is set up to take advantage essentially of a loophole in U.S. chip policy towards China, which is, Okay, we’re not gonna sell the most advanced chips to China, but we will sell them to a company that sets up in another country and operates a data center that then rents that capacity to China . So she’s already kind of navigating in this vulnerable space that U.S. policy towards China doesn’t account for. And the fact that she then, or is already, a Chinese intelligence asset just adds to probably the concern that I could imagine U.S. officials would have had, because her company essentially exists to make money by circumventing the very policies the U.S. is trying to create to keep China from getting ahead in the AI race. Rosin: What would China have demanded of Alice Huang? What would have been the list they gave to Alice Huang, like, We want X , Y , and Z? Harris: You could imagine it would be pretty long, but maybe some that would be at the top: What’s the next-generation chip that’s coming, and how powerful is it? What are the conversations going on inside the Trump administration about where they might be amenable to loosening the restrictions on the sales of chips to us? Can you implant this idea in Jensen Huang’s head that he should go to the president and say X , Y , or Z ? It’s tempting to say, Tell us everything that you can , right? But if she’s an asset who’s being directed, there will be pretty specific things that China wants to know, and that list will be curated by all of the different people in that space in China who have an objective, which might be getting access to better chips or trying to understand what the next wave of technological development is so that they can get ahead of that. Warzel: Well, I also think, too—we don’t know the exact relationship between Alice and Jensen: how often they met, and in which places they met, whether they were alone or not. Was she alone with his phone? There are things like that. He is call buddies with Donald Trump. What potentially does she have access to? Are the Nvidia IT and device policies as strict when he is in Singapore as they are when he is in the United States? There’s so many questions about that. There’s potential for things like data collection in there. He has god-tier access to his own company, presumably. I think everything is on the table, is essentially the point. Rosin: Charlie, I’m curious what the fear of China getting ahead looks like from inside the tech industry. I understand why the U.S. government fears it. How do tech leaders talk about that? Warzel: Well, I think one of the fears of China getting ahead is that China is also much more inclined to have these open-source models—these models that you don’t have to pay for in the same way that level the playing field, so to speak, between the OpenAIs and the Anthropics of the world, in which they are charging a pretty penny, especially for enterprise access. When the Chinese model DeepSeek came onto the scene sort of unannounced, and showed that it was just as powerful, if not in some cases a little more powerful, than some of the, quote, unquote, “frontier models” from these American companies, it called briefly into question the entire economic model of all of these companies. But I think the way that these AI companies—they call themselves “labs”—the way that they work is: They train, they build up these models, then they release them to the public. But the things that they are training tend to be a lot more powerful. And those models can be very dangerous if they’re released to different people, but also if they’re used in any kind of way. And so the idea is: If China were to leapfrog the U.S. in the capability with the training and the things like this, they would be playing effectively a different game. And the capabilities can work in an exponential fashion. And so if you are six months ahead, that doesn’t sound like a lot to most people on the outside of this business, but it could mean living in a completely different paradigm of the technology. Rosin: Shane, is there a worst-case scenario, like: We find out X happens, and everything falls apart ? In this moment when all this information is emerging, what would be the “Oh my God” scenario? Harris: One would be: The president was told Jensen Huang has relayed private discussions that the two of you had to this woman, and she has delivered it gift-wrapped to Chinese intelligence, and they know what our AI policy is gonna be next year . And the president said , Eh, whatever . And that he did nothing about it. The president’s lack of response to what he was told, reportedly, twice, begs the question of, Well, what exactly was he told? So that’s one. Another worst-case scenario could be when Alice Huang is in a private room hanging out with Jensen Huang and he gets up to excuse himself for a few minutes and she puts a device on his computer, and the MSS is up entirely in the communications of the CEO of Nvidia for the past year and a half and sees everything that’s going across his email. The intelligence agency would be crazy not to at least contemplate trying to do that if they had an asset with intimate contact to someone like Jensen Huang. So those would be worst-case scenarios. That essentially, China, either through direct access to his devices or because he is, in the course of pillow talk, talking about trade secrets or his conversations with White House officials, that that’s all going back to Beijing, and they’re basically just sitting there and reading it. [ Music ] Rosin: Charlie, and listeners, I’m going to do something a little unusual now. We actually taped another version of this conversation earlier on Tuesday, before the latest news broke. And I want to play you a bit of the audio from that taping. So this is Charlie, on Charlie. Charlie, are we ready for Charlie? Warzel: ( Laughs .) Always. Always ready for myself. Rosin: ( Laughs .) Okay, go ahead. Warzel: Well, it’s funny because when you were asking Shane that question of what’s the worst scenario, my version of it is that there’s no choice but for Huang to step down. I think that’s a nightmare scenario for the economy, also probably for Nvidia. I think it’s very important to think about Huang in the sense of this entire boom. And going back to what I said at the outset of this is that he is believed to be one of the visionaries who’s made this happen, whose decisions in changing Nvidia’s supply chain, but also in utilizing how these chips can power this artificial-intelligence investment and scale things up—he is credited with a lot of that. He is extremely well respected. And the confidence collapse that happens when you take that person out of it, I think it would at least cause some very, very serious turmoil. And I think one way to look at all of this—especially if you’re a cynic about the AI build-out—is that it is, if not a house of cards, it is a Jenga pile, right? Or it is something in which there are so many load-bearing bricks, and if you take one of them out, the whole thing can come tumbling down. And I think it’s not a ridiculous thing to say that Nvidia is one of those load-bearing bricks. [ Music ] Rosin: Charlie, that nightmare scenario you describe might suddenly be happening now. So what do you think? Warzel: I think that no one should have to listen to themselves from two days ago, frankly. Rosin: ( Laughs .) Warzel: I think that this is a little bit of a scary moment. Maybe it’s scarier than we think. I wanna separate the morality of what he’s done here, and the recklessness of what he’s done, from just the meat and potatoes—like how the market and how this industry might react. I’ve heard of Nvidia being referred to as the “bank of Nvidia,” recently, since this has come out—this idea that they put so much investment into this sector, and that so much of that investment in this sector is so closely tied to his ability, Jensen’s ability, to make these deals. But the fact that this industry is funded and supplied by this one guy in this one company, and the idea of him not being at the center of it is fully destabilizing, I think. I really and truly believe that. This analyst, Dan Ives, said that Nvidia would be worth 25 percent to 30 percent less without Jensen Huang. This may be the craziest story in the AI era since ChatGPT launched, truly. What I sense and what I hear from people in the industry about all of this is that we have taken one of the Jenga blocks out, potentially, and does the tower hold up? Does it not? We’re gonna find out in the next weeks and months. Rosin: Well, Charlie, Shane, thank you so much for joining me today. Harris: Thank you. Warzel: Thanks for having me. Rosin: This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Rosie Hughes and Jinae West. It was edited by Kevin Townsend. Fact-checking by Sam Fentress. Rob Smierciak engineered and provided original music. We also had music from Breakmaster Cylinder. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. Listeners, if you enjoy the show, you can support our work and the work of all Atlantic journalists when you subscribe to The Atlantic at TheAtlantic.com/Listener . I’m Hanna Rosin. Thank you for listening.

title: The Scandal Is Bigger Than Jensen Huang
zh_title: 丑闻比黄仁勋更大
summary: 尽管英伟达的完整故事仍在浮出水面，但最令人震惊的消息可能不是美国最具影响力的人工智能高管黄仁勋与一名疑似中国间谍有牵连。高级政府官员可能已收到有关危险的警告，但仍继续依赖他来指导美国的技术未来。美国的战略在很大程度上依赖于强大的私营部门参与者，政府不能简单地认为这些参与者的激励措施将符合国家利益。 2025年5月，黄被拍到在T餐厅用餐
content:
尽管英伟达的完整故事仍在浮出水面，但最令人震惊的消息可能不是美国最具影响力的人工智能高管黄仁勋与一名疑似中国间谍有牵连。高级政府官员可能已收到有关危险的警告，但仍继续依赖他来指导美国的技术未来。美国的战略在很大程度上依赖于强大的私营部门参与者，政府不能简单地认为这些参与者的激励措施将符合国家利益。 2025 年 5 月，黄被拍到与据称是中国国家安全部资产的黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 在台北用餐，并与黄爱丽有过恋爱关系。今年五月，特朗普总统飞往北京会见中国国家主席习近平。据报道，国务卿马可·卢比奥在飞行中向特朗普通报了这一情报。但这一令人震惊的信息并没有阻止特朗普带黄仁勋出访或将他视为重要顾问。在阿拉斯加加油站，黄与代表团会合。他在通常由总统高级助手占用的小屋里与埃隆·马斯克聊天。黄面前的桌子上放着分发给客人的白宫品牌巧克力：好时之吻。
当一行人抵达北京时，黄从飞机上出来，与特朗普、卢比奥和其他高级官员一起走红地毯，这是黄与总统关系密切以及他对政府的中国和人工智能政策影响力的有力象征。[阅读：经济中心的丑闻]特朗普的本能是支持他的人。这些爆料并没有动摇总统的明显信念，即英伟达的领导人是不可或缺的。但截至撰写本文时，《华尔街日报》报道称，英伟达董事会可能正准备罢免黄仁勋。政府在处理这一问题方面正面临重大质疑：彭博社报道称，2025 年夏末，Nvidia 的总法律顾问就该公司对 Megaspeed 的调查联系了商务部高级官员，而商务部较低级别的员工在如何进行涉及 Nvidia 的调查方面面临着不同寻常的限制。周日，当被问及是否应该按照警告采取行动时，特朗普回答说：“不，我不这么认为。”黄是我们所说的“双鸽子”。他曾说过“对华鹰”标签是“耻辱的徽章”。当美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）主播法里德·扎卡里亚（Fareed Zakaria）问黄仁勋，美国还是中国赢得人工智能竞赛是否重要时，他说：“我认为并不重要。”同样，黄对灾难性人工智能风险的警告不以为然。
这些观点与 Anthropic 的达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 的观点形成鲜明对比，后者是“双鹰”，将中国视为关键的国家安全威胁，并警告人工智能可能对人类构成生存风险。两人都坚称，他们的立场反映了他们对美国国家利益和人工智能未来的理解。但他们的分歧也符合他们的商业利益。英伟达通过向全球尽可能多的客户销售芯片来获利，黄仁勋也曾游说美国限制向中国出售先进人工智能芯片。相比之下，Anthropic 则受益于让中国企业尽可能远离前沿。具有讽刺意味的是，这两个人的生意是交织在一起的。与许多其他领先的人工智能开发商一样，Anthropic 使用 Nvidia 芯片。人工智能竞赛通常被理解为企业之间、国家之间的竞争，

【原文 English Original】
Although the full Nvidia story is still emerging, the most alarming revelation may not be that Jensen Huang, America’s most influential AI executive, was involved with a suspected Chinese spy. It may be that senior administration officials were warned about the danger and nevertheless continued relying on him to guide the United States’ technological future. American strategy has come to depend, to an extraordinary degree, on powerful private-sector actors whose incentives the government cannot simply assume will align with the national interest. In May 2025, Huang was photographed dining in Taipei with Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese Ministry of State Security asset with whom he had a romantic relationship. This past May, President Trump flew to Beijing to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping. In flight, Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly briefed Trump on the intelligence. But that shocking information did not stop Trump from bringing Jensen Huang on the trip or treating him as a key adviser. At a refueling stop in Alaska, Huang rendezvoused with the delegation. He chatted with Elon Musk in a cabin usually occupied by the president’s senior aides. On the table in front of Huang sat the White House–branded chocolates given out to guests: Hershey’s Kisses . When the group arrived in Beijing, Huang emerged from the plane to walk the red carpet alongside Trump, Rubio, and other top officials, a powerful symbol of Huang’s closeness to the president and his influence on the administration’s China and AI policy. [ Read: A scandal at the center of the economy ] Trump’s instinct was to stand by his man. The revelations did not shake the president’s apparent conviction that Nvidia’s leader was indispensable. But as of this writing, The Wall Street Journal has reported that the Nvidia board may be preparing to oust Huang. The administration is facing major questions about its handling of the issue: Bloomberg has reported that in late summer 2025, Nvidia’s general counsel contacted senior Commerce Department officials about the company’s investigation into Megaspeed, and lower-level Commerce employees faced unusual restrictions on how they could pursue inquiries involving Nvidia. Asked on Sunday whether he should have acted on the warning, Trump replied, “No, I don’t think so.” Huang is what we might call a “double dove.” He famously said the “China hawk” label was a “badge of shame.” When the CNN anchor Fareed Zakaria asked Huang if it matters whether the United States or China wins the AI race, he said, “I don’t think it does.” Similarly, Huang dismisses warnings about catastrophic AI risks. These views contrast with those of Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, who is a “double hawk,” seeing China as a crucial national-security threat and warning that AI could pose an existential risk to humanity. Both men insist that their positions reflect their understanding of American national interests and AI’s future. But their disagreements also align with their commercial interests. Nvidia profits from selling chips to as many customers globally as it can, and Huang has lobbied against American restrictions on the sale of advanced AI chips to China. By contrast, Anthropic benefits from keeping Chinese firms as far behind the frontier as possible. Ironically, the two men’s businesses are intertwined. Anthropic, like many other leading AI developers, uses Nvidia chips. The AI race is generally understood as a competition among firms and between nations, but it is also a battle of ideas. At its center is what I have called the dream of “ AI primacy ”: the conviction that advanced AI could give the United States a permanent advantage over its rivals, restoring an era of unchallengeable American dominance. But that vision depends on the questionable assumption that technological power accumulated by American companies can be reliably converted into power exercised by the American government. American and Chinese leaders speak of two rival technological systems, but those systems are in fact not entirely separate. They are interdependent, entangled through the movement of technology, capital, information, and people. Beijing has officially refused to import the large quantities of Nvidia chips that the Trump administration has approved for sale—but Megaspeed and similar companies operate on a business model that demonstrates how reliant Chinese AI firms remain on computing power from abroad. Some use data centers in Southeast Asia to get around U.S. restrictions. Silicon Valley executives, for their part, talk of a zero-sum race between America and China even as American AI companies rely on talent from China. These interdependencies create economic opportunities but also avenues for espionage, coercion, and manipulation. And the more the AI race depends on sprawling networks of companies, customers, and governments, the more influence accrues to the handful of individuals who sit at their intersection. [ Rogé Karma: Democrats have no coherent plan for AI ] Technological supremacy and national power do not always pull in the same direction. A remarkably small circle of executives and officials make the decisions that will shape AI’s future and the geopolitical competition around it. The power of these individuals is fast escaping the reach of the institutions responsible for guarding against technological and geopolitical risks. The Information suggests that Alice Huang exploited her access to Jensen Huang to help Chinese companies obtain billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department reportedly delayed action against Megaspeed, even as other agencies pressed for restrictions. Axios reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last week about why Megaspeed had not been added to a government list of restricted entities, following months of interagency warnings about the company. The unanswered questions now extend well beyond the affair itself: Did the relationship influence Nvidia’s commercial decisions, causing the company to allocate products to Megaspeed rather than American firms? Did Nvidia’s political influence compromise the government’s ability to enforce its own rules? Some leaders of the AI race speak as though their inventions will allow humanity to transcend its limitations—and perhaps give one country power over all others. Yet the people guiding this transformation remain vulnerable to the oldest weaknesses of human nature: ambition, vanity, fear, greed, desire. The era they are making is defined by the collision between superhuman ambitions and human frailty. The lesson of this scandal is not simply that these people are fallible. It is that we need institutions capable of checking their influence and managing the consequences of their mistakes before these individuals become too powerful to be held accountable. *Illustration image sources: Joel Saget / AFP / Getty; Feng Li / Getty; Finn Gomez / Getty; Sean Gallup/Getty.

title: U.S. Transfers Unmanned Surface Vessels to Philippine Marine Corps
zh_title: 美国向菲律宾海军陆战队转让无人水面舰艇
summary: 2023 年 10 月 26 日，美国第五舰队第 59 特遣部队的一艘 MARTAC T-38 Devil Ray 无人水面舰艇在阿拉伯湾航行。美国海军照片 菲律宾海军陆战队上周在苏比克湾接收了两艘美国制造的无人水面舰艇，这是华盛顿加强马尼拉在南中国海和吕宋海峡的不对称能力的努力的一部分。 11月4日，两艘海上战术系统T38魔鬼鱼无人水面艇被转移到苏比克湾的菲律宾海军陆战队。 “今天标志着我们继续努力加强菲律宾能力的又一个有意义的步骤
content:
2023 年 10 月 26 日，美国第五舰队第 59 特遣部队的一艘 MARTAC T-38 Devil Ray 无人水面舰艇在阿拉伯湾航行。美国海军照片 菲律宾海军陆战队上周在苏比克湾接收了两艘美国制造的无人水面舰艇，这是华盛顿加强马尼拉在南中国海和吕宋海峡的不对称能力的努力的一部分。 11月4日，两艘海上战术系统T38魔鬼鱼无人水面艇被转移到苏比克湾的菲律宾海军陆战队。菲律宾海军陆战队副司令准将说：“今天标志着我们在不断努力加强菲律宾海军陆战队能力方面又迈出了有意义的一步，特别是在群岛海岸防御领域。”根据美国海军学院新闻提供的文字记录，巴亚尼·库拉明将军出席了仪式。据美国海军学院新闻六月报道，菲律宾海军陆战队被定为继菲律宾海军之后下一支接收无人机的部队。马尼拉海军陆战队处于南海争端的最前线，驻守着被大批中国正规军和准军事部队包围的前哨基地。一位熟悉此事的美国国防官员也强调了菲律宾陆军通过该计划接收无人机的可能性。据美国海军学院新闻了解，该部队正在寻求扩大其群岛海岸防御计划中监测和控制受威胁目标的能力。
近年来，菲律宾海军陆战队装备了“布拉莫斯”岸防巡航导弹，并被转移到从苏禄海到吕宋海峡的战略海上交通线。横须贺亚太研究委员会东南亚地区项目主任查理·布朗告诉美国海军学院新闻，无人机的转移使海军陆战队能够“在广阔且竞争日益激烈的海域”保持警觉。布朗表示：“这是建立可信的群岛防御能力的一个重要因素：不一定要与对手的平台相匹配，而是利用技术、信息共享和分布式能力使菲律宾的海上途径更加透明，领土防御更具弹性。”在马尼拉和北京之间因南海争议领土问题出现一系列紧张局势后，五角大楼正在采取更广泛的努力，以提高菲律宾的领海意识，这些无人机是在该行动的范围内进行的。 2023年以来，中国和菲律宾军队多次就对方声称拥有主权的多个浅滩和岛礁发生冲突。马尼拉为对抗中国军队而进行的新生现代化努力得到了美国和日本越来越多的支持。总部位于佛罗里达州的海上无人机制造商 Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. 很早就被任命为菲律宾海军提供第一批无人水面航行器。目前，海军第一支无人水面航行器的核心由一艘 T38 Devil Ray 和四艘 MANTIS T12 组成。
海军陆战队无人水面艇被转移到 MARTAC 的新苏比克湾设施。根据公司发布的消息，无人机卓越中心旨在培训菲律宾无人机操作员并为魔鬼鱼库存零件。 MARTAC 发布的新闻稿称：“CoE 还将为当地创造就业机会和建立合作伙伴关系，以增强菲律宾在未来几年部署大型 USV 舰队的能力。”今年夏天，总部位于密西西比州的自主 USV 公司 Ocean Aero, Inc. 向菲律宾海军交付了四架 Triton 无人机。美国-菲律宾倡议目前的重点是提供海域意识

【原文 English Original】
A MARTAC T-38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessel, attached to U.S. 5th Fleet’s Task Force 59, sails in the Arabian Gulf, Oct. 26, 2023. US Navy photo The Philippine Marine Corps received two American-made unmanned surface vessels last week at Subic Bay as part of Washington’s efforts to bolster Manila’s asymmetric capabilities in the South China Sea and Luzon Strait. On Nov. 4, two Maritime Tactical Systems T38 Devil Ray USVs were transferred to the Philippine Marine Corps at Subic Bay. “Today marks another meaningful step in our continuing effort to strengthen the capabilities of the Philippine Marine Corps, particularly in the field of archipelagic coastal defense,” said PMC Deputy Commandant Brig. Gen. Bayani Curaming at the ceremony, according to a transcript provided to USNI News. The Philippine Marine Corps was slated as the next force to receive drones after the Philippine Navy, USNI News reported in June . Manila’s Marines are at the forefront of South China Sea disputes, manning outposts surrounded by swarms of Chinese regular and paramilitary forces. An American defense official familiar with the matter also highlighted the possibility of the Philippine Army receiving drones through the program. The force is looking to expand its capabilities to monitor and hold targets under threat in its Archipelagic Coastal Defense plan, USNI News understands. In recent years, Philippine Marines have been equipped with BrahMos coastal defense cruise missiles and were relocated to strategic sealines of communication from the Sulu Sea to the Luzon Strait. Charlie Brown, the Director of the Yokosuka Council on Asia Pacific Studies’ Southeast Asia Regional Program, told USNI News that the drone transfer enables the Marines in maintaining awareness “across a large and increasingly contested maritime domain.” “This is an important element of building a credible archipelagic defense capability: not necessarily matching an adversary platform for platform, but using technology, information-sharing and distributed capabilities to make the Philippines’ maritime approaches more transparent and its territorial defense more resilient,” said Brown. These drones are under a broader effort from the Pentagon to enhance Philippine maritime domain awareness following a renewed series of tensions over disputed territories in the South China Sea between Manila and Beijing. Since 2023, Chinese and Philippine forces have repeatedly clashed across several shoals and reefs claimed by the other. Manila’s nascent modernization efforts to contend with Chinese forces has seen increased American and Japanese backing . Florida-based sea drone manufacturer Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. was tapped early on to provide the Philippine Navy’s first USVs. Currently, the core of the sea service’s USV Unit One is composed of one T38 Devil Ray and four MANTIS T12s. The Marine Corps USVs were transferred at MARTAC’s new Subic Bay facility. According to a company release, the drone center of excellence is designed to train Philippine drone operators and stock parts for the Devil Rays. “The CoE will also enable creation of local jobs and partnerships to build Philippines capabilities for deploying a large USV fleet over the next several years,” reads the MARTAC release. Over the summer, Mississippi-based Autonomous USV firm Ocean Aero, Inc. delivered four Triton drones to the Philippine Navy. The U.S.-Philippine initiative is currently focused on delivering maritime domain awareness capabilities to address significant gaps around the Southeast Asian archipelago of more than 7,600 islands. However, the program plans to integrate one-way attack drones and other lethal capabilities by 2027.

title: UPDATED: USS South Dakota Command Triad Relieved After October Grounding, Congressman Says

content:
2026 年 6 月 30 日，在康涅狄格州格罗顿的新伦敦海军潜艇基地，弗吉尼亚级核动力快速攻击潜艇南达科他号 (SSN-790) 指挥变更仪式上，鸣放 11 响礼炮，迎接第 2 潜艇大队指挥官梅尔文·史密斯少将的到来。丹尼尔·古德温接替了中校的职务。伯恩斯·C·W·布朗 (Burnes C.W. Brown) 担任南达科他州指挥官。美国海军照片 美国海军照片 南达科他号航空母舰 (SSN-790) 的指挥三合会上个月因搁浅事件而被拆除，根据一名国会议员的声明。根据众议院海上力量和投送部队小组委员会高级成员乔·考特尼（康涅狄格州民主党人）众议员和众议院军事委员会高级成员亚当·史密斯（华盛顿州民主党人）周四发布的一封信，该潜艇的指挥官、执行官和艇长于 10 月 14 日被解除指挥权，据称此次解除是由于搁浅事件。指挥官。据康涅狄格州新伦敦《每日报》报道，丹·古德温被解除南达科他州指挥官职务。根据五角大楼发布的消息，古德温于 2026 年 6 月接任南达科他州指挥官。一位知情人士告诉美国海军学院新闻，在潜艇舵软接地后，三合会被移除。信中称，议员们从一名记者要求对解雇事件发表评论的请求中得知，他们松了口气。
近一个月后，众议院军事委员会尚未收到任何有关解雇或潜在事件的通知。 2026 年 6 月 30 日在康涅狄格州格罗顿新伦敦海军潜艇基地的快速攻击潜艇码头上举行南达科他号 (SSN-790) 号航空母舰指挥变更仪式后，南达科他号 (SSN-790) 舰长丹尼尔·古德温被送上岸。信中写道：“海军部未能向国会通报这些事件是不可接受的。”致代理海军部长曹洪和海军作战部长达里尔·考德尔上将。海军通常会向国会通报海上事件、事故和指挥三合会的解散。 “海军缺乏透明度留下了许多悬而未决的问题，不仅涉及发生了什么，还涉及导致三合会解散的事件对南达科他州的结构健康、船员的福祉的影响，以及该事件是否暴露了必须解决的标准程序培训方面的任何系统性问题。由于海军未能沟通，本应成为信息共享标准的演习反而引发了人们对海军对透明度的承诺以及对与国会建立富有成效的工作关系的承诺的质疑。”这封信。一名国防官员向美国海军学院新闻证实了这一消息。
海军发言人承认了美国海军学院新闻的提问，但没有立即发表评论。 目前尚不清楚南达科他州是否受损。南达科他号于 2019 年服役，是海军最先进的潜艇之一，也是新型潜艇技术的试验台。美国海军学院新闻 2016 年报道称：“这艘船采用了使船舶更安静的涂层、更安静的喷水推进器以及安装在船体两侧的附加声纳，以提高船员探测敌方船只和潜艇的能力。”美国攻击潜艇上一次重大搁浅是在 2021 年。在南海执行任务时，美国海军康涅狄格号 (SSN-21) 与一艘水下潜艇相撞。

【原文 English Original】
11-gun salutes are fired for the arrival of Rear Adm. Melvin Smith, Commander, Submarine Group 2, during the Virginia-class nuclear-powered fast attack submarine USS South Dakota (SSN-790) Change of Command Ceremony at Naval Submarine Base New London in Groton, Connecticut, June 30, 2026. Cmdr. Daniel Goodwin relieved Cmdr. Burnes C.W. Brown as Commanding Officer of South Dakota. US Navy photo USS South Dakota (SSN-790) command triad was removed last month following a grounding incident, according to a statement from a member of Congress. The submarine’s commanding officer, executive officer and chief of the boat were relieved from command on Oct. 14, with the relief allegedly attributed to a grounding incident, according to a letter released Thursday by Reps. Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, and Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee. Cmdr. Dan Goodwin was relieved as commander of South Dakota , according to a story in the Day newspaper based in New London, Conn. Goodwin assumed command of South Dakota in June of 2026, according to a Pentagon release . A source familiar told USNI News the triad removal followed a soft grounding of the submarine’s rudder. Lawmakers learned of the relief from a reporter’s request for comment on the dismissal, according to the letter. Nearly one month later, no notifications of the firings or the underlying incident had been made to the House Armed Services Committee. Cmdr. Daniel Goodwin, commanding officer of USS South Dakota (SSN-790) is piped ashore following the USS South Dakota (SSN-790) change of command ceremony that was held June 30, 2026, onboard the fast attack submarine pierside at Naval Submarine Base New London in Groton, Conn. US Navy photo “The Department of the Navy’s failure to communicate these incidents to Congress is unacceptable,” reads the letter, which is addressed to Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao and Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle. The Navy typically informs Congress of at-sea incidents, accidents and dismissals of command triads. “The Navy’s lack of transparency leave many outstanding questions about not only what occurred, but the impact of the events leading the triad’s dismissal on the structural health of South Dakota , the well-being of the crew, and whether the incident laid bare any systemic issues with training to standard procedures that must be addressed. As a result of the Navy’s failure to communicate, what should have been a standard exercise in information sharing has instead raised questions about the Navy’s commitment to transparency and its commitment to a productive working relationship with Congress,” reads the letter. A defense official confirmed the removals to USNI News. A Navy spokesperson acknowledged a question from USNI News but did not immediately provide a comment. It’s unclear whether South Dakota was damaged. Commissioned in 2019, South Dakota is one of the Navy’s most advanced submarines and serves as the test bed for new submarine technology. “The boat received coatings that keep the ship quieter, a quieter water jet propulsor and additional sonars mounted on the sides of the hull to increase the crew’s ability to detect enemy ships and submarines,” USNI News reported in 2016 . The last major grounding of a U.S. attack submarine was in 2021. While operating in the South China Sea, USS Connecticut (SSN-21) collided with an underwater sea mount, resulting in extensive damage to the boat. The submarine is still undergoing repairs.

title: 习近平为何清洗自己的人？——托里吉安谈恐惧、党性与接班政治

content: 编按 2026 年 10 月下旬，约 300 名中共中央委员在北京闭门召开二十届五中全会，会议确认了数十名中央委员被除名。自 2022 年开始第三个任期以来，习近平对党内高层发动了毛泽东时代以来最彻底的清洗：中央军委领导成员几乎被清洗一空，除他本人外，只剩下主管调查工作的张升民；仅过去一年，就有三名政治局委员落马，其中包括他长期倚重的军委副主席张又侠。清洗为何走到这一步？美利坚大学教授托里吉安（Joseph Torigian）是习仲勋英文传记《党的利益高于一切》（The Party’s Interests Come First）的作者。他在布鲁金斯学会的播客节目中给出的解释值得重视：在习近平的政治观念里，干部犯错从来不是能力或环境的问题，而是“政治觉悟”出了问题，是对事业失去了信仰，因此不能轻罚，只能清除。与毛时代不同的是，被清洗的人不再有平反的可能，“要么上升，要么彻底出局”，体制内的恐惧也因此更深。托里吉安同时提醒，观察 2027 年党代会前的接班政治，应当保持分析上的谦逊。斯大林和毛泽东身后的历史表明，接班斗争的胜出者未必是政策最得人心的人，结果往往取决于谁能操纵模糊的规则；而在规则模糊的时候，关键在于谁能调动军队和政治警察。 来源 The Beijing Brief 播客第 18 期：“Why is Xi Jinping purging leaders of his own party?”，布鲁金斯学会约翰·桑顿中国中心，2026 年 11 月 10 日。主持人：乔纳森·钦（Jonathan A. Czin，布鲁金斯 Michael H. Armacost 外交政策讲席研究员）、何瑞恩（Ryan Hass，桑顿中国中心主任）；嘉宾：托里吉安（Joseph Torigian，美利坚大学国际服务学院副教授）。 原文与完整文字稿： https://www.brookings.edu/articles/why-is-xi-jinping-purging-leaders-of-his-own-party/ Members of the Communist Party of China Central Committee attend a press conference following the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in Beijing, China, October 30, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov 摘要 一、谣言、恐惧与“不再平反”的清洗 托里吉安开篇就强调要保持“分析上的谦逊”。社交媒体上关于中共高层的传言，大多是因为人们“愿意相信”才流传开来，而且没有人能够证实或证伪。张又侠落马前的传言碰巧属实，但“停了的钟一天也能对两次”。他长期查阅美国档案，发现其中充斥着某位领导人已经去世、某地发生政变之类的假消息。在他看来，历史的作用在于提供时间纵深，帮助我们在证据极少的情况下提出假设，而不是去鉴别某一条传言是否可靠。 他还指出了本轮清洗与毛时代相比的变与不变。1959 年彭德怀被整肃时，毛泽东说“我们不用苏联人那种办法解决问题”，意思是不搞处决。习仲勋被整了 16 年，单独关押期间，他每天来回踱步、数着步数，为的是等到党“回心转意”那一天，身体还能撑得住。如今，处决依然罕见，但平反也不再出现。毛泽东尚且认为蒙冤受难是一种“淬炼”，熬过去的人会更加努力地赢回党的信任；习近平却从来没有对谁说过：“你经历了这么多苦难，我们反而更倚重你。”犯错的代价极其沉重，而且几乎不可能全身而退，这说明体制内的恐惧有多深。托里吉安说：“在美国，你不喜欢自己的政党，可以退出；对这些人来说却没有退路，要么上升，要么彻底出局。”据毛泽东的保健医生记述，当年高层很多人因为压力过大而出现类似的病症，不少人靠安眠药度日。在他看来，这些全会提醒我们，身处这个正与美国竞争的组织之中，究竟是怎样一种处境。 二、犯错即“政治觉悟”问题：清洗背后的意识形态逻辑 托里吉安认为，理解这轮清洗的关键，在于习近平对“党的自我治理”的执着。习近平相信，只有共产党才能把这个国家组织起来、实现“复兴”。他还宣称，党解决了一个连马克思、恩格斯都“没有想到”的问题：一个长期执政的政权，如何保持纯洁，保持理想信念。而谁有“党性”（即相信党的使命，把比个人更大的事业放在生命的中心），由他本人来判定。于是，犯错不再是在复杂环境中的失误，而是“信仰出了问题”，必须清除，以“纯洁队伍”。这种逻辑在党史话语中根深蒂固，习仲勋也说过类似的话：身体再健康，只要沾上一丁点资产阶级个人主义的病菌，也可能一夜之间垮掉。换言之，清洗永远没有可以停下来的那一天。五中全会的文件一方面充满胜利者的口吻，另一方面又强调反腐败斗争“依然严峻复杂”，还用植树护林作比：坏树要不断地拔，林子要不断地管。 地方官员因此左右为难。文件既要求扎紧“制度的笼子”，又批评形式主义、官僚主义；既要求与党中央保持高度一致，又说这与担当作为、因地制宜“并不矛盾”。习近平还认为党内存在大量“两面人”，表面拥护，实际不然。这样一来，甄别干部只能依靠主观的、非法律的间接信号。谁受惩罚、罚得多重、罪名如何定性，取决于党在具体情境下的利益，取决于最高领导人想要达成什么，而通常只有他一个人掌握全部的盘算。托里吉安说，他研究中国政治最核心的困惑是：为什么极其忠诚的人会一再被清洗？问题从来不在于下属对领袖失去信任，而在于领袖对下属失去信任，“权力是自上而下流动的”。他估计，习近平自认为远没有走到毛时代那一步，分寸拿捏得恰到好处；别人或许认为他走得太远，但这本身就是一种主观判断。 三、张升民与张又侠：清洗政治的两张面孔 张升民是这轮清洗的受益者，已升任军委副主席并进入政治局。他曾撰文说，高级军官应当少交朋友，要认识到任何交往都带有政治性质。毛时代一起打天下的老干部彼此往来随意，常常因此惹祸；如今这一代军官，大概不会在饭局上议论习近平。托里吉安引用赵紫阳 1980 年代的一句话：中国政治说到底，就是当面一套，背后一套。获得提拔的人，有的兴奋不已，以为自己会是例外；有的则心怀恐惧，因为位子越高越容易出错，最大的愿望不过是“软着陆”。人们常以为列宁式体制中的人都是权力最大化者，总在伺机扳倒习近平；但实际上，许多人只想平平安安地熬过去。而即便万分小心，也未必能保住自己。 张又侠的经历有其特殊之处。他的父亲在文革中原本像个“不倒翁”，常常站在整人的一边，处境比习仲勋好得多，却在文革末期犯下大错，最终以失势告终。而张又侠在父亲失势的情况下，仍然上了对越作战的前线。这种忠诚，或许正是习近平所看重的。习近平喜欢讲，当年其他太子党不愿去基层时，他去了；不过那时他的父亲正位高权重，而张又侠的父亲已经失势。两人的人生故事，就这样耐人寻味地对应起来。然而到了今年，这位习近平如此倚重的人，也到了“该走的时候”。托里吉安由此想到毛泽东在 1959 年彭德怀被整肃前后说过的一句话：“我的思想、我的理智和我的感情始终是一致的。”常人很难做到这一点，但毛泽东做到了；在他看来，习近平大概也是如此。 四、军队大换血与台海风险 主持人钦（Jonathan A. Czin）指出，张又侠只是众多案例中的一个，解放军出身的中央委员大多已被免职。他把自己的观察方法比作印象派绘画：盯着一个点看，只会看得眼花；退后一步，才能看清整体图案。对军队领导层进行如此彻底的代际清洗，会带来什么影响？托里吉安坦言只能推测。在清洗的阴影下，解放军高层恐怕很难把多少心思放在台海作战上，很难说清洗对战备没有影响。但在习近平看来，解放军过去之所以成功，恰恰在于它有正确的“政治觉悟”，因此必须以极大的力度反腐。对他来说，腐败不只是浪费的问题，更关乎在精英权斗、国内动乱或对美战争中，军队是否听他指挥。一支忠诚的、经过政治教育、有斗志的军队，是绝对必要的条件。即便短期内要付出代价，也必须这么做，“他其实别无选择”。托里吉安还提到一些流传出来的对军队讲话：即使从军事上看打台湾是划算的，也不该打；但如果出于政治原因必须打，即使军事上不划算，也必须打。他对习近平的判断是（他强调这只是推测）：在台湾问题上，习近平最在乎的是能够说自己“把事情往前推进了”，局面比他接手时更好；就目前而言，做到这一点大概就够了。但威权领导人向来会做他们认为能够得逞的事。 五、接班政治：斯大林与毛泽东身后的教训 托里吉安比较了斯大林和毛泽东死后的权力交接。两者的相似之处在于，那都是一场关于谁握有谁的把柄、谁整过谁、谁的旧账最多的较量，处处充满猜忌和恐惧。想要胜出，既要在混战中占据有利位置，又不能动摇党的根基。他从新档案中得出的一个重要结论是：接班斗争通常并不存在“政策最受欢迎的人胜出”这样的遴选机制，也没有一个明确的群体来做决定。结果取决于如何操纵模糊的规则：谁抢先一步，谁能左右在哪里决策、由谁决策。而当规则模糊时，“最终说了算的是手里有枪的人”。这并不是说军队会扮演“造王者”，关键在于谁能使用军队，而不是军队使用谁。 至于习近平是否会终身执政，托里吉安怀疑他自己也还没拿定主意，因为每一个选项都不理想。要避免身后出现混战、国家被带往完全不同的方向，就得在生前选定一个信得过的副手，考察他是否能干、是否听话，并给他时间积累权力和威望。这正是毛泽东在斯大林死后的思路：“不能让赫鲁晓夫那样的人出现”，于是选了刘少奇。刘少奇对毛忠诚，但毛很难相处，他像一位“哲学王”，会一连几个月不露面，而且疑心很重，结果这条路没有走通。毛晚年考虑过多位接班人，最终选定华国锋，而华国锋斗不过邓小平。邓小平“同样挽救了革命，但走的是一条与毛的设想截然不同的路”。如果不选接班人，身后就可能出现他书中所描述的那种局面。影响习近平决定的因素包括：身边副手的政治手腕、其他国家的接班经验（他们一直密切关注俄罗斯）、对美关系是否稳定、经济能否撑住，以及他本人的健康状况。这些外人很难看清，恐怕他本人也不容易看清。托里吉安还补充了一个耐人寻味的观察：习近平认为，西方搞垮共产党国家靠的不是暴力，而是用消费主义和物质主义拉拢体制内的人。在他看来，苏联在戈尔巴乔夫手中解体，并不是制度本身出了问题，而是美国一场成功的渗透行动的结果。这个难题过去从来没有人找到好的答案，习近平身边的人恐怕也清楚，它对中国体制的稳定意味着多大的风险。托里吉安说：“我可不想和这样一个人共处一室：他选人的最高标准是‘和我一样’，同时又有充分的理由怀疑，你只是在他面前装成那样的人。” 节目最后，托里吉安提醒华盛顿，不要高估“派系”分析。共事关系确实非常重要，党内也历来存在相互庇护、相互提携的山头，这正是习近平深恶痛绝的，因为它会侵蚀军队的战斗力，也会让人们对这个体制失去信心。但共事并不等于交情。彭德怀经常对张又侠的父亲大发雷霆，还不止一次撤过他的职；周恩来也曾把他骂哭。但这并不意味着他会因此对谁不忠。习仲勋和王震在 1950 年代初曾因新疆政策发生激烈冲突，后来却成了亦敌亦友的关系。共事经历能帮助我们留意可能发生的事情，但它能告诉我们的，远比想象的要少。他最后说，党史永远只是“最新的一稿”，“我们应当把彼此的分歧当作人民内部矛盾来处理，而不是当作政治觉悟错误的表现”。

title: November 12: An Enduring Testament to the Uyghur People’s Will to Be Free
zh_title: 11 月 12 日：维吾尔人民自由意志的永恒见证
summary: CUS 新闻稿 立即发布 2026 年 11 月 12 日 Contact@uyghurstudy.org Uyghurstudy.org 维吾尔研究中心 (CUS) 纪念 11 月 12 日，纪念东突厥斯坦伊斯兰共和国成立 93 周年（1933 年在喀什宣布）和东突厥斯坦共和国成立 82 周年（1933 年在喀什宣布成立）。古尔贾，1944 年）。我们向所有为民族自决而献出生命的烈士表示崇高的敬意。 11 月 12 日被全球维吾尔人庆祝为“东突厥斯坦国庆日”，这代表了维吾尔人两次宣布的决心
content:
CUS 新闻稿 立即发布 2026 年 11 月 12 日 Contact@uyghurstudy.org Uyghurstudy.org 维吾尔研究中心 (CUS) 纪念 11 月 12 日，纪念东突厥斯坦伊斯兰共和国成立 93 周年（1933 年在喀什宣布）和东突厥斯坦共和国成立 82 周年（1933 年在喀什宣布成立）。古尔贾，1944 年）。我们向所有为民族自决而献出生命的烈士表示崇高的敬意。 11 月 12 日被全球维吾尔人庆祝为“东突厥斯坦国庆日”，它代表了该地区人民两次宣称的主宰自己命运的决心。这个日期是东突厥斯坦在中国控制之外的独特国家地位和主权的明确历史证据。历史背景 1930 年代初期的民族解放斗争最终于 1933 年 11 月 12 日在喀什宣告成立东突厥斯坦伊斯兰共和国，霍贾·尼亚孜担任总统，萨必提·阿卜杜勒巴齐·达毛拉担任总理。外部地缘政治压力导致共和国于 1934 年崩溃，但它却留下了不朽的遗产，制定了宪法、国徽和不可磨灭的主权身份。十一年后，在古尔加抵抗之后，1944 年 11 月 12 日，在总统阿里汗·托雷的领导下，东突厥斯坦共和国宣告成立。
1949 年 8 月，包括艾哈迈德詹·卡西米、阿卜杜勒克里姆·阿巴斯、伊沙克别克·穆诺诺夫和达列尔汗·苏古尔巴耶夫在内的主要领导人在飞往北京途中的一次飞机失事中丧生。此后不久，中国人民解放军 (PLA) 占领了该地区，开始了持续的占领。今日维吾尔人 过去77年来，中国共产党执行了旨在根除维吾尔族身份的系统性政策。今天，这场运动构成了针对东突厥斯坦维吾尔族、哈萨克族、吉尔吉斯族和其他穆斯林突厥民族的持续种族灭绝。大量文件证实了集中营的大规模拘禁、强迫劳动、强制绝育、强迫儿童分离、破坏文化遗产、将宗教活动定为犯罪以及消灭维吾尔语。联合国人权事务高级专员办事处 2022 年 8 月的评估确认，这些违法行为可能构成国际罪行，特别是危害人类罪。中国对维吾尔人的镇压通过跨国监视、恐吓和家庭调节扩展到全球。 […] 无数成员的帖子《11 月 12 日：维吾尔人民自由意志的持久见证》首先出现在维吾尔研究中心。

【原文 English Original】
CUS Press Release For Immediate Release November 12, 2026 Contact@uyghurstudy.org Uyghurstudy.org The Center for Uyghur Studies (CUS) commemorates November 12, marking both the 93rd founding anniversary of the East Turkistan Islamic Republic (proclaimed in Kashgar in 1933) and the 82nd founding anniversary of the East Turkistan Republic (proclaimed in Ghulja in 1944). We honor with solemn remembrance all martyrs who sacrificed their lives for national self-determination. Observed globally by Uyghurs as “East Turkistan National Day,” November 12 represents the twice-proclaimed resolve of the people of the region to govern their own destiny. This date stands as clear historical evidence of East Turkistan’s distinct statehood and sovereignty outside of Chinese control. Historical Background The national liberation struggle in the early 1930s culminated in the proclamation of the East Turkistan Islamic Republic in Kashgar on November 12, 1933, with Hoja Niyaz as President and Sabit Abdulbaqi Damolla as Prime Minister. External geopolitical pressures led to the republic’s collapse in 1934, yet it established an enduring legacy, defining a constitution, national emblem, and indelible sovereign identity. Eleven years later, following the Ghulja resistance, the East Turkistan Republic was proclaimed on November 12, 1944, under the leadership of President Alikhan Tore. In August 1949, key leaders – including Ahmetjan Qasimi, Abdulkerim Abbas, Ishaqbek Munonov, and Dalelkhan Sugurbayev – perished in a plane crash en route to Beijing. Shortly thereafter, the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) occupied the region, initiating the ongoing occupation. Uyghurs Today Over the past 77 years, the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has executed systematic policies aimed at eradicating Uyghur identity. Today, this campaign constitutes an ongoing genocide targeting Uyghurs, Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, and other Muslim Turkic peoples in East Turkistan. Extensive documentation confirms mass internment in concentration camps, forced labor, coercive sterilization, forced separation of children, destruction of cultural heritage, criminalization of religious practices, and the eradication of the Uyghur language. The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights’ August 2022 assessment affirmed that these violations may constitute international crimes, specifically crimes against humanity. China’s repression of Uyghurs extends globally through transnational surveillance, intimidation, and family conditioning. title: 秦伟平参加Katy ISD两所学校退伍军人节活动：致敬军人、倾听教师，关注下一代教育
summary: 纵览中国｜美国德克萨斯州Katy消息｜2026年11月12日 2026年11月11日美国退伍军人节当天，美国海军退伍军人、Katy ISD学区董事会第六选区候选人秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）先后参加了德克萨斯州Katy独立学区（Katy Independent School District，简称Katy ISD）两所学校举办的退伍军人节活动，分别是Shafer Elementary小学和Seven Lakes Junior High初中。 秦伟平随后通
content: 纵览中国｜美国德克萨斯州Katy消息｜2026年11月12日 2026年11月11日美国退伍军人节当天，美国海军退伍军人、Katy ISD学区董事会第六选区候选人秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）先后参加了德克萨斯州Katy独立学区（Katy Independent School District，简称Katy ISD）两所学校举办的退伍军人节活动，分别是Shafer Elementary小学和Seven Lakes Junior High初中。 秦伟平随后通过个人Facebook、X（原Twitter）及Substack等平台发布活动照片和文字，分享当天的经历与感受。从校园对退伍军人的致敬，到与一线教育工作者的交流，两场活动也使教师薪酬、特殊教育支持以及学校人才队伍建设等问题成为他关注的议题。 Shafer Elementary：学生以歌声和荣誉墙向退伍军人致敬 当天，秦伟平首先参加了Shafer Elementary举办的退伍军人节庆祝活动。 根据秦伟平在社交媒体发布的介绍，学校在图书馆为退伍军人、现役军人、军人家长、教师及家庭成员准备了早餐和咖啡，让来自不同家庭和服役背景的社区成员有机会交流。 活动特别设置了退伍军人荣誉墙，展示与学校有关的退伍军人照片及个人故事，其中也包括秦伟平本人，以及目前仍在美国军队服役的学生家长。学生们还亲手制作了表达感谢的留言，向曾经和正在服役的军人及其家庭致敬。 当天的学生表演也是活动的重要环节。学生们演唱了代表美国不同军种的歌曲。当相应军种的歌曲响起时，曾在该军种服役的退伍军人起立，全校师生则以掌声表达敬意。 此外，学校Student Council（学生会）的学生代表还朗诵了一首献给退伍军人的诗歌。 秦伟平在个人文章中表示，学生们真挚的表演和表达令他十分感动。他也特别向学校校长Gonzales及全体教职员工表达感谢，肯定学校为活动所作出的准备和安排。 秦伟平表示，自从离开美国海军以来，今年已经是他连续第四年参加学校举办的退伍军人节活动。他注意到，今年活动的规模比往年更大，也看到了更多退伍军人家庭和现役军人家庭参与学校及社区生活。 他在文章中向学生们表达了自己的期望：珍惜学习机会，勇敢追求梦想，充分利用自由社会所提供的成长机会。他认为，孩子们能够安心学习、快乐成长并自由追求未来，正是几代美国军人长期服役、努力守护的重要意义。 Seven Lakes Junior High：与教育工作者交流，关注教师待遇 随后，秦伟平还参加了Seven Lakes Junior High举办的退伍军人节活动。 与Shafer Elementary以学生表演和校园庆祝为主的活动氛围不同，这次活动也为秦伟平提供了与其他退伍军人家长、教师及学校社区成员交流的机会。 在秦伟平发布的另一篇文章中，他特别提到，与一位从事特殊教育工作的代课教师交谈，给自己留下了深刻印象。 据秦伟平转述，这位教师主要协助有特殊学习及行为需求的学生，工作需要高度的耐心、责任感和持续投入，但她向他表示，自己的时薪只有13美元。 这一情况引起了秦伟平对学校基层教育人员薪酬和人才留任问题的关注。 他在文章中提出一个问题：如果教育工作者承担的工作责任和实际压力，无法得到相应的薪酬与支持，学区又该如何吸引和留住足够优秀、富有责任感的教育人才？ 秦伟平认为，教师和学校工作人员是公共教育体系的重要组成部分，他们的工作不仅关系到课堂教学，也直接影响学生的学习体验、特殊教育支持以及学校整体运行。 需要指出的是，13美元时薪是秦伟平根据与一位代课教师的个人交谈所转述的信息，目前并非经过学区公开薪酬资料独立核实的普遍薪酬标准。不同岗位、雇佣方式和工作安排之间可能存在差异。 不过，这次交流反映出他希望进一步了解基层教育工作人员实际工作状况的意愿，也将教师薪酬与人才招聘、留任问题带入其对当地教育治理的讨论。 从军旅服役到教育公共事务：关注服务与下一代 秦伟平曾在美国海军服役，退役后继续从事美国联邦政府公共服务工作。目前，他居住在Katy社区，是三个Katy ISD在校学生的父亲。 2026年11月11日，他选择在美国退伍军人节正式宣布竞选Katy ISD Board of Trustees, Position 6（学区董事会第六选区），计划参加2027年5月的学区董事会选举。 在其近期公开发布的竞选信息和个人文章中，教育工作者支持、学生发展、校园环境、学区财政管理及社区沟通等问题，均是其重点关注的方向。 对于此次参加两所学校的活动，秦伟平将其视为一次与学校社区深入交流的机会。他认为，退伍军人节不仅是纪念军人服役经历的日子，也让社区有机会重新认识公共服务、家庭责任以及下一代成长所需要的社会支持。 他在Substack文章中写道，作为一名美国海军退伍军人和三个孩子的父亲，他希望将对服务与责任的理解延伸到社区教育事务中。如果当选学区董事，他将关注教师薪酬和工作支持，倾听教师及学校工作人员的意见，并推动学区政策和资源配置更加贴近学生与教育一线的实际需求。 秦伟平表示，教师待遇不仅是劳动报酬问题，也关系到学区能否吸引和留住教育人才，以及学生能否获得稳定、持续的教育支持。 教师支持与学生发展：地方教育治理中的长期议题 Katy ISD是休斯顿西部地区重要的公共教育学区，学校教育涉及学生、家长、教师、行政人员及不同背景的社区家庭。 教师招聘与留任、特殊教育资源、学校工作人员待遇以及教育资源配置，都是地方学区治理中需要持续关注的议题。 从Shafer Elementary学生为退伍军人准备的荣誉墙和表演，到Seven Lakes Junior High一线教育工作者分享的工作经历，秦伟平在同一天接触到学校社区的不同侧面。 前者体现了学校对军人及其家庭的尊重，后者则使教师工作条件和基层教育支持问题进入他的视野。 秦伟平在文章最后向两所学校的领导、教师、工作人员、家长及学生表达感谢，并表示，希望继续倾听社区不同群体的声音，为改善Katy ISD教育环境和学生成长机会贡献力量。 他将当天的感受概括为：致敬曾经服役的人，关爱今天教书育人的人，投资明天的下一代。 这也成为他在2026年退伍军人节参加两所学校活动后，对公共服务与地方教育责任所作出的个人总结。 相关信息： 秦伟平竞选职务：Katy ISD Board of Trustees, Position 6 选举时间：2027年5月 竞选网站： https://www.weipingqintx.com/ 个人动态：X、Facebook及Substack平台。
