content:
内容摘要：10 月份乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯，损坏了 Yandex、VK、Sberbank 和俄罗斯联邦税务局运营的数据中心，扰乱了数字服务，并引发了将基础设施从莫斯科地区搬迁到远东的讨论。随着人们越来越担心俄罗斯系统落后于美国和中国模式，莫斯科正在着手正式确定其人工智能（AI）政策。新的人工智能立法于 9 月生效。俄罗斯官员将国内人工智能视为国家主权问题，但计算基础设施和技术人员的短缺，以及外国人工智能模型的日益使用，威胁着莫斯科发展有竞争力的国内行业的努力。 10 月 8 日，乌克兰无人机袭击了俄罗斯最大科技公司 Yandex 旗下的大型数据中心之一，导致该公司在全国各地的服务大规模中断。罢工使该公司的云服务进入紧急模式，客户不得不将数据转移到其他云系统（Habr，10 月 12 日）。 Yandex 数字生态系统内的其他服务需要数周时间才能恢复（T-J，10 月 26 日）。
VK Company Limited 是另一家控制着领先的俄语社交媒体网站 VKontakte 和 Odnoklassniki、国家消息系统 Max 以及俄罗斯领先的电子邮件服务 Mail.ru 的大型科技公司，最近其数据中心也遭受了损害，俄罗斯最大的金融机构 Sberbank 也是如此（CNews，10 月 18 日）。这些攻击只是克里姆林宫在继续推动完全数字主权时面临的众多困难之一。这些 10 月份的攻击符合乌克兰无人机针对俄罗斯数据中心的更广泛模式，包括那些属于联邦组织的数据中心，例如下诺夫哥罗德的国家税务局（Nastoyashee Vremya，10 月 23 日）。 Ozon 是一家电子商务公司，被认为是俄罗斯的亚马逊，自 8 月以来一直面临着针对其仓库的无人机袭击（Omskinform，10 月 28 日）。这些攻击对俄罗斯发展安全和主权科技行业的努力产生了严重后果。俄罗斯科技行业正在呼吁加强安全性，一些人正在讨论将数据中心迁往远东的可能性，因为目前 75% 的商业数据中心位于莫斯科州（Techora，10 月 27 日）。技术媒体讨论的其他选择包括将数据中心移至哈萨克斯坦。 Yandex 尚未面临西方的全面制裁，使其有可能将基础设施转移到国外（Habr，10 月 12 日）。
对俄罗斯科技行业的物理攻击正值克里姆林宫越来越担心该国人工智能（AI）的未来。俄罗斯杜马成立了一个委员会来解决人工智能问题，由执政的统一俄罗斯党副秘书长、俄罗斯“外国代理人”法的发起人之一亚历山大·西迪亚金（Aleksandr Sidyakin）领导，该法名义上旨在减少外国在该国的影响力，并压制独立媒体、非政府组织和非系统性政治反对派（Meduza， 9 月 24 日）。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，俄罗斯的主权将取决于该国开发自己的国内人工智能的能力（RBC，4 月 10 日）。人工智能在俄罗斯对乌克兰战争中的快速发展彻底改变了战场，减少了

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia in October damaged data centers operated by Yandex, VK, Sberbank, and Russia’s Federal Tax Service, disrupting digital services and prompting discussion of relocating infrastructure from the Moscow region to the Far East. Moscow is moving to formalize its artificial intelligence (AI) policy as concerns grow that Russian systems are falling behind U.S. and Chinese models. New AI legislation entered into force in September. Russian officials view domestic AI as a matter of national sovereignty, but shortages of computing infrastructure and skilled personnel, alongside growing use of foreign AI models, threaten Moscow’s efforts to develop a competitive domestic sector. Ukrainian drone strikes on October 8 struck one of the large data centers belonging to Yandex, Russia’s largest tech company, leading to massive interruptions in the company’s services around the country. The strikes pushed the company’s cloud services into emergency mode, and clients had to move their data to other cloud systems ( Habr , October 12). Other services within the Yandex digital ecosystem required weeks to recover ( T-J , October 26). VK Company Limited—another major tech company which controls the leading Russian-language social media sites VKontakte and Odnoklassniki, the national messaging system Max, and Mail.ru, Russia’s leading e-mail service—also recently faced damage to its data centers, as did Sberbank, Russia’s largest financial institution ( CNews , October 18). These attacks underscore just one of the many difficulties facing the Kremlin as it continues to push for complete digital sovereignty. These October attacks fit into a broader pattern of Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian data centers, including those belonging to federal organizations, such as the National Tax Service in Nizhnyi Novgorod ( Nastoyashee Vremya , October 23). Ozon, an e-commerce company that is considered Russia’s answer to Amazon, has faced continued drone attacks targeting their warehouses since August ( Omskinform , October 28).  The attacks have had serious consequences for Russia’s attempts to develop a secure and sovereign tech sector. The Russian technology industry is calling for additional security, and some are discussing potentially relocating data centers to the Far East, as 75 percent of commercial data centers are currently located in Moscow oblast ( Techora , October 27). Other options discussed in the technology press include moving data centers to Kazakhstan. Yandex has not faced comprehensive Western sanctions, enabling it to potentially move infrastructure abroad ( Habr , October 12). The physical attacks on Russia’s technology sector come as the Kremlin becomes more concerned about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) in the country. The Russian Duma formed a committee to address AI issues, headed by Aleksandr Sidyakin, deputy secretary general of the ruling United Russia party and one of the initiators of Russia’s “foreign agents” law, which nominally aimed to reduce foreign influence in the country and suppressed independent media, non-governmental organizations, and non-systemic political opposition ( Meduza , September 24). Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that Russia’s sovereignty will depend on the country’s ability to develop its own domestic AI ( RBC , April 10). The rapid development of AI use in Russia’s war against Ukraine has completely altered the battlefield, reducing the applicability of lessons from previous wars, according to Russian Deputy Defense Minister General Yunus-Bek Evkurov in an August interview ( RBC , August 10). The first legislation specifying Kremlin policies for the development of domestic models entered into effect in September, though some provisions will not take effect until March 2027. “Sovereign” AI models must use only domestic technologies under the law, while “national” models can use foreign components and open-source solutions ( RBC , August 31). “Sovereign” models, according to Sidyakin, must “conform to Russian spiritual and moral values” ( RIA Novosti , October 27). Moscow is concerned that Russian AI is falling behind models from the United States and the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Sberbank President German Gref estimated that Russian AI was a half-year behind Beijing’s systems and expressed fears that this lag will continue ( RBC , September 24). This announcement followed news that PRC models were the second and third most popular models among Russian clients using domestic cloud platforms, with the use of PRC AI growing elevenfold year-on-year ( Kommersant , August 13). Surveys published in the summer found that respondents from 79 percent of 100 major Russian companies reported too few AI specialists and 91 percent lacked sufficient server infrastructure ( ITZine , July 29).  These concerns about AI development are compounded by evidence of brain drain. Arkadii Volozh, the original founder of Yandex, immigrated to the Netherlands in 2024 after criticizing Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, taking 1,000 engineers with him, along with plans to develop a company specializing in infrastructure for AI systems. His assets were then sold to Russian investors for $5.4 billion ( IncRussia , July 16). The Kremlin is subsidizing the development of domestic AI by offering tax breaks to small and medium enterprises that adopt domestic solutions, but the country will need 89,000 AI specialists by 2030, according to estimates presented at a tech conference by former Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitrii Gorgenko ( Vedomosti , September 21; Ekspert , October 24). The new AI legislation is part of a broader shift toward Russian digital sovereignty. This push includes a “sovereign” internet and national network defense system (see EDM , May 20). Russia faces serious challenges, including developing national AI systems that can compete with U.S. and PRC versions while protecting its technology infrastructure from Ukrainian strikes. Further attacks leading to extended online interruptions would likely undermine support for the war effort and disrupt Russia’s digital economy. A major relocation of technology infrastructure to the Far East would likely require heavy state support and the development of an ecosystem to support the data centers, both serious undertakings for an economy that is facing stagnation (see EDM , November 2).  The post Russia’s Push for AI Sovereignty Faces Setbacks appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Military Makes up Majority of Expulsions at Fifth Plenum
zh_title: 五中全会驱逐人员中军人占多数
summary: 内容提要：五中全会的三分之二驱逐事件与中华人民共和国（PRC）的国防机构有关。被开除干部的背景表明，无论是专业资格还是与习近平的长期个人关系都无法提供可靠的保护以免受纪律调查。正在进行的清洗主要影响的是中国人民解放军（PLA）军队。与此同时，空军没有被驱逐，这强化了这样的评估：空军可能会在重建后的解放军最高指挥部中获得更大的影响力。正式开除
content:
内容提要：五中全会的三分之二驱逐事件与中华人民共和国（PRC）的国防机构有关。被开除干部的背景表明，无论是专业资格还是与习近平的长期个人关系都无法提供可靠的保护以免受纪律调查。正在进行的清洗主要影响的是中国人民解放军（PLA）军队。与此同时，空军没有被驱逐，这强化了这样的评估：空军可能会在重建后的解放军最高指挥部中获得更大的影响力。全会上正式开除的决定表明，无理缺席党内重大活动是政治垮台的明确信号：16名被开除的官员中有11人缺席2025年10月的四中全会，另外两人随后立即从公众视野中消失。中国反腐败监管机构正在密切关注国防工业领导人。进一步的调查可能会扰乱航空航天和造船业，给中国的国防工业基础和军事现代化带来新的挑战。中国共产党中央委员会最近召开了五中全会，重点关注党内纪律、权力集中、思想强化和人事调整（《中国简报》，11 月 3 日；IISS，11 月 4 日）。
其中一项突出进展是开除33名中央委员的党籍（IDSS报，11月4日）。其中涉及16名武装部队军官和17名文职干部，其中六人与国防国有企业关系密切（《早报》，10月30日）。尽管中央军委副主席张升民进入政治局引起了分析人士的广泛关注，但大规模驱逐前军官和国防工业领导人也同样重要，甚至更重要——揭示了对中国武装部队状况的有意义的见解。军队开除 在被开除军官名单中名列前茅的是前解放军将军、中央军委副主席张又侠。作为中越边境冲突期间的一名功勋指挥官，张在2017年至2026年担任中央军委副主席期间还一直担任政治局委员，是最高军事和民事决策机构之间的关键纽带。尽管张与习近平有着长期的关系，但他不知何故与中国领导人发生了冲突，并于 2026 年 1 月被免职并被拘留，与他在一起的还有刘振立。刘振立是一位陆军将领、战争英雄，曾在中央军委任职，并于 2022 年至 2026 年担任中国人民解放军参谋长。
中央于 2026 年 9 月首次开除张、刘的党籍，随后在五中全会上重申了这一决定（中国最高法院，9 月 21 日）继张、刘之后的是中国人民解放军海军上将王仁华，他于 2019 年至 2025 年担任中央军委政法委员会书记，负责军事司法系统和反间谍工作。王于 2025 年 10 月失踪，一切都没有发生。直到最近他被开除出中共，才听说过他（财新，2025 年 10 月 28 日）。刘青松，海军上将，2023年至2025年任东部战区政委。他与去年10月被清洗的东部战区司令员林向阳一起工作（《中国简报》，2025年11月25日）。刘就是其中之一

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Two thirds of the Fifth Plenum’s expulsions are tied to the national defense apparatus in the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The backgrounds of expelled cadres suggest that neither professional credentials nor longstanding personal relationships with Xi offer reliable protection against disciplinary investigations. The ongoing purge mainly affected the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Army. The absence of Air Force expulsions, meanwhile, reinforces the assessment that the service may gain greater influence in the reconstructed PLA high command. Expulsions formalized at the plenum suggest that unjustified absence from major Party events is an unambiguous signal of political downfall: Eleven of the 16 expelled officers were absent from the Fourth Plenum in October 2025, while two others disappeared from public view immediately afterwards. Chinese anti-corruption watchdogs are keeping defense industry leaders under close scrutiny. Further investigations could disrupt the aerospace and shipbuilding sectors, creating new challenges for the PRC’s defense industrial base and military modernization. The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) Central Committee recently concluded its Fifth Plenum, focusing on internal Party discipline, the centralization of power, ideological reinforcement, and personnel reshuffles ( China Brief , November 3; IISS , November 4). One outstanding development was the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members from the Party ( IDSS Paper , November 4). These involved 16 armed forces officers and 17 civilian cadres, six of whom were closely linked with defense state-owned enterprises ( Zaobao , October 30). Although the promotion of Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin (张升民) to the Politburo attracted considerable analyst attention, the mass expulsion of former military officers and defense industry leaders is of equal, if not greater, importance—revealing meaningful insights on the state of the Chinese armed forces. Armed Forces Expulsions At the top of the list of expelled military officers is former People’s Liberation Army (PLA) general and CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia (张又侠). As a decorated commander during the Sino-Vietnamese border conflict, Zhang also served on the Politburo throughout his tenure as CMC vice chairman from 2017–2026, serving as a critical link between top military and civilian decision-making organs. Despite his longstanding ties with Xi, Zhang somehow ran afoul of the Chinese leader and was removed and detained in January 2026, alongside Liu Zhenli (刘振立), a fellow Army general and war hero who served on the CMC and as the PLA chief of staff from 2022–2026. The Central Committee first expelled Zhang and Liu from the Party in September 2026, before it reaffirmed the decision at the Fifth Plenum ( China Supreme Court , September 21) Following Zhang and Liu is PLA Navy admiral Wang Renhua (王仁华), who served as secretary of the CMC political and legal affairs commission from 2019–2025, in charge of the military justice system and counterespionage. Wang disappeared in October 2025 and nothing was heard of him until his recent expulsion from the CCP ( Caixin , October 28, 2025). Liu Qingsong (刘青松) is a Navy admiral who served as the political commissar of the Eastern Theater Command from 2023–2025. He worked with the disgraced Eastern Theater Command Commander Lin Xiangyang (林向阳), who was purged in October last year ( China Brief , November 25, 2025). Liu was one of at least 18 officers absent at the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 ( Sing Tao Daily , October 27, 2025; BBC , November 7, 2025). His whereabouts remained unknown until his expulsion at the Fifth Plenum. Army general Huang Ming (黄铭) first vanished from public view in July 2025 and was absent at the subsequent Fourth Plenum. The commander of the Northern Theater Command from 2024–2025, Huang was once regarded as a promising leader within the Army ( Zaobao , August 3, 2024). His expulsion at the Fifth Plenum, however, sealed his fate. Li Qiaoming (李桥铭) was another elite Army general with a long list of professional accomplishments. He rose from a simple soldier to become the fourth commander of the PLA Army in 2022. Yet Li was missing in action during the Fourth Plenum last year and was booted out of the National People’s Congress (NPC) in February 2026 ( Xinhua , February 26). His expulsion from the CCP at the Fifth Plenum made him the third Army commander to be purged since the post was created in 2015 amid changes to the military’s organizational structure known as the “Deepening National Defense and Military Reform” (深化国防和军队改革). Army general Li Wei (李伟) was the third political commissar of the now-disbanded Strategic Support Force and then became the first political commissar of the Information Support Force, founded in 2024 to succeed the Strategic Support Force’s cyber capabilities ( Zaobao , April 20, 2024; China Brief, April 26, 2024 [ a ], [ b ]). Like Li Qiaoming, Li Wei failed to attend the Fourth Plenum and was removed from the NPC in February 2026. He was formally expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. Zhang Hongbing (张红兵) spent most of his career in the PLA Army before transferring to the People’s Armed Police in 2022 as its political commissar, attaining the rank of general. He disappeared from public view for most of 2025, including the Fourth Plenum, and was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum ( Zaobao , December 24, 2025). Wang Haijiang (汪海江) was regarded as a capable Army officer who fought in the Sino-Vietnamese border conflict ( China Brief , June 7). He spent over a decade serving at senior PLA posts in Xinjiang and Tibet before becoming the Western Theater Command commander in 2021. He did not attend the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 and was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. The same fate befell Army lieutenant general Yang Cheng (杨诚), the political commissar of the Xinjiang military district from 2020–2025 who most likely maintained working relations with Wang Haijiang ( Caixin , April 6, 2021). Three former heads of CMC departments were also expelled following their absence from last year’s Fourth Plenum. They were Army lieutenant general Wang Peng (王鹏), who headed the CMC training and administration department from 2021–2025; Army lieutenant general Liu Faqing (刘发庆), who led the CMC national defense mobilization department from 2021–2025; and Navy vice admiral Zhao Xiaozhe (赵晓哲), who previously oversaw the CMC science and technology department. Separately, Army lieutenant general Zhang Lin (张林), director of the CMC logistics support department from 2022–2025, was removed from the NPC last October and expelled at the Fifth Plenum ( Zaobao , October 16, 2025). Last but not least, Army lieutenant generals Zhong Shaojun (钟绍军) and Fang Yongxiang (方永祥) were both considered confidants of Xi. Zhong assisted Xi since the latter’s tenure in Zhejiang in the early 2000s ( VOA , August 29). After Xi came to power, he brought Zhong into the PLA as a senior colonel, despite having no military experience, to manage the crucial CMC chairman’s office that supported Xi’s daily work schedule ( China Brief , September 14). Zhong subsequently became director of the CMC general office that provided administrative and logistical support to all CMC members, before eventually serving as political commissar of the National Defense University. He vanished in October 2025 and was removed from the NPC in August 2026, prior to his expulsion from the Party in October ( Zaobao , October 29). Fang succeeded Zhong in leading both the CMC chairman’s office and CMC general office, indicating a high level of trust that Xi had in him ( SCMP , October 26, 2024). Like many previously mentioned officers, Fang failed to attend the Fourth Plenum, with no news regarding his whereabouts until his expulsion from the CCP at the recent Fifth Plenum. Defense Industry Expulsions Other than military officers, Sun Shaopin (孙绍骋), former minister of veterans affairs from 2018–2022, was also expelled from the Party ( Caixin , January 29). Moreover, one third of the 17 civilian cadres expelled at the Fifth Plenum were associated with state-owned defense enterprises. At the top of the expulsion list was Lei Fanpei (雷凡培). He had a long career in the country’s aerospace industry, rising from an ordinary designer to become chairman of the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). From 2018–2022, Lei was the chairman of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC) ( World Ships , October 31). From 2022–2025, Lei served as the deputy director at the Office of Central Military-Civil Fusion Development Commission (中央军民融合发展委员会办公室) ( Zaobao , October 31, 2024). Despite being an experienced technocrat and crucial link between defense companies and policymakers, Lei was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. Several other senior leaders from the defense sector were expelled at the same time. They include former chairman of the China National Nuclear Corporation Yu Jianfeng (余剑锋); former chairman of CASC Yuan Jie (袁洁), who was removed in 2024 likely in connection with the Rocket Force investigations that year ( Radio Free Asia , April 15, 2024); Zhang Zhongyang (张忠阳), former chairman of CASC and head of the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology, the country’s largest research, development, and production institution for carrier rockets and missile systems ( Zaobao , January 30, 2024); Wen Gang (温刚), former chairman of Norinco and CSSC ( Caixin , October 30); and Jin Donghan (金东寒), an engine and marine propulsion research specialist and former president of Shanghai University and Tianjin University. Jin spent decades researching engines for the PRC’s defense industry and led the CSSC’s Shanghai Marine Diesel Engine Research Institute that specializes in marine diesel and gas engines, power systems, electrical and automation systems, and energy equipment ( 163 , January 15). Scope of Purge Shows Inter-Service Political Priorities As the largest PLA service, the Army predominated among those expelled, accounting for 11 of the 16 military officers. The Navy follows with three officers, Information Support Force and the People’s Armed Police each account for one. Neither the Air Force nor Rocket Force saw any expulsions this time. While the lack of Rocket Force expulsions may be linked to the broad purges that decimated its top leadership in 2023 and the subsequent years, the absence of Air Force expulsions again highlights this service as the least affected by the purges so far. This reinforces the author’s previous assessment that the Air Force is set to gain influence within the reconstructed PLA high command, as its senior leadership remains comparatively intact ( The Diplomat , August 11). The professional backgrounds of expelled officers also reveal important patterns in the direction of the purge. Military officers with extensive command experience constitute seven cases while political commissars account for six, followed by three defense technocrats. This shows that the commanders and commissars of major PLA organizations are most at risk. The authorities appear to make no distinction between commanders or commissars when conducting investigations. In comparison, defense technocrats, who tend to stay in the background, seem to be less affected by the current campaign. Interestingly, three expelled officers had close personal ties with Xi, with relations dating back years, if not decades. But this did not save them from being purged, indicating that Xi does not tolerate any malfeasance or signs of disloyalty among military officers, regardless of their personal relations with him. Fourth Plenum Absences as a Potential Purge Indicator Another recurring theme is the connection between the expelled and the Fourth Plenum. Out of 16 officers expelled at the Fifth Plenum, 11 were absent from the Fourth Plenum in October 2025, with two more—Wang Renhua and Zhong Shaojun—disappearing from public view immediately after the gathering. This suggests that these 13 officers had likely been detained and placed under investigation around the time of the Fourth Plenum. This sequence teaches us that absence from key Party meetings is an early warning sign of political trouble and missing individuals are likely to end up as purge victims. It is worth noting that several other officers absent from the Fourth Plenum have not yet been expelled. They include Commander of the Southern Theater Command Wu Ya’nan (吴亚男); Political Commissar of the Central Theater Command Xu Deqing (徐德清); Commander of the PLA Navy Hu Zhongming (胡中明), and Political Commissar of the PLA Rocket Force Xu Xisheng (徐西盛) ( Sing Tao Daily , October 27, 2025; BBC , November 7, 2025). Despite having no news and public appearance since the Fourth Plenum, events at the Fifth Plenum suggest that they have met their downfall. Turning to the defense industry, the affiliations of the expelled executives reveal a clear concentration of those associated with CASC and CSSC. Others were linked to the China National Nuclear Corporation, Norinco, and key research institutions developing missiles and marine engines. There may be parallels between the depth of corruption within these corporations and the quality of their equipment, echoing concerns previously raised about Rocket Force vulnerabilities ( CNA , January 11, 2024). As investigations are likely to expand in these sectors, the disruptions could have negative consequences for the PRC’s defense industrial base and military modernization. Conclusion The armed forces and defense industry cadres constitute a two-third majority of Fifth Plenum expulsions, an extraordinary development when personnel involved in national defense only account for a minority within the entire Party-state elite. While the rise of CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin reestablished formal communications between the Politburo and the PLA, the Fifth Plenum’s expulsions offer broader insights into the state of the PLA. As Xi reconstructs the high command, the Fifth Plenum reminds us that trust between the commander-in-chief and his generals remains low ( The Diplomat , July 6). While it is not difficult to appoint new people to top posts, building confidence and rapport is a long-term project that might be undermined by frequent leadership instability. The post Military Makes up Majority of Expulsions at Fifth Plenum appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Nemaska pause clouds Rio Tinto’s Quebec lithium plans
zh_title: 内马斯卡暂停令力拓魁北克锂计划蒙上阴影
summary: 据《蒙特利尔日报》报道，力拓（LSE、ASX、NYSE：RIO）位于魁北克的 Nemaska 锂工厂的建设计划将在 2027 年之前暂停，这使其计划于 2028 年开工受到质疑。该报援引公司信函报道称，员工周三被告知，工作可能会在 2028 年恢复，尽管这一消息尚未得到证实。魁北克省经济发展部长办公室在早些时候的报告中确认，截至 12 月的裁员人数为 68 人。 “这一决定并不反映力拓或内马斯卡锂业董事会承诺的任何减少，”力拓在放慢速度时表示。
content:
据《蒙特利尔日报》报道，力拓（LSE、ASX、NYSE：RIO）位于魁北克的 Nemaska 锂工厂的建设计划将在 2027 年之前暂停，这使其计划于 2028 年开工受到质疑。该报援引公司信函报道称，员工周三被告知，工作可能会在 2028 年恢复，尽管这一消息尚未得到证实。魁北克省经济发展部长办公室在早些时候的报告中确认，截至 12 月的裁员人数为 68 人。 “这一决定并不反映力拓或 Nemaska Lithium 董事会承诺的任何减少，”力拓在 3 月份放慢建设速度时表示。据该报报道，较长的停顿引发了人们对魁北克省投入该项目的 12 亿加元（合 8.46 亿美元）公共资金回报率的质疑。 3月份该工厂已完成70%以上，当时力拓表示预计总体时间表不会发生重大变化。资金压力贝坎库尔项目是魁北克尝试建立电池供应链的一部分，该供应链将当地开采的矿物转化为更高价值的材料。贝坎库尔位于蒙特利尔东北约 150 公里处，与三河市隔圣劳伦斯河相望。力拓在 2 月份将其持股比例增至 54% 后取得了直接管理控制权。魁北克省通过魁北克投资局持有剩余 46% 的股份。当时，魁北克承诺追加高达2亿美元的股权，力拓承诺在2026年为其魁北克锂业务提供超过3亿美元的资金。
该省将其贡献描述为最终投资，并表示力拓已承诺在 2028 年将该工厂投入使用。最新报道的暂停将使之前预定的首次生产年份的建设重启变得不确定。锂暴跌 BMO 周四援引 Fastmarkets 的消息称，亚洲碳酸锂现货价格已从 5 月份的每公斤 25 美元以上跌至每公斤 12.90 美元。 BMO表示，需求增长疲软以及非洲和中国供应不断扩大给市场带来压力。力拓还在审查该工厂锂辉石的长期供应，锂辉石是一种用于制造氢氧化锂的含锂矿物。该公司一直在评估 Nemaska 的 Whabouchi 项目及其全资拥有的 Galaxy 项目，以确定最佳来源。 2月份，力拓预计供应审查将在今年上半年完成。 BMO周四表示，这两个项目之间的选择仍未解决。周四上午，力拓股价在纽约证券交易所交易中下跌 1.51%，至 83.72 美元，该公司估值约为 1,360 亿美元。去年该股的价格区间为 68.70 美元至 112.58 美元。

【原文 English Original】
Construction of Rio Tinto ’s (LSE, ASX, NYSE: RIO) Nemaska lithium plant in Quebec is set to remain on hold through 2027, putting its planned 2028 start in doubt, according to Le Journal de Montréal. Employees were told Wednesday that work could resume in 2028, although that was unconfirmed, the newspaper reported , citing a company letter. Quebec’s economic development minister’s office had confirmed 68 layoffs extending through December in earlier reporting. “This decision does not reflect any reduction in commitment from Rio Tinto or from the Board of Nemaska Lithium,” Rio said when it slowed construction in March. The longer pause raises questions about the return on C$1.2 billion ($846 million) of public funding that Quebec has put into the venture, according to the newspaper. The plant was more than 70% complete in March, when Rio said it did not foresee major changes to the overall timetable. Funding pressure The Bécancour project forms part of Quebec’s attempt to build a battery supply chain that converts locally mined minerals into higher-value materials. Bécancour lies about 150 km northeast of Montreal, across the St. Lawrence River from Trois-Rivières. Rio took direct management control in February after increasing its interest to 54%. Quebec holds the remaining 46% through Investissement Québec. At the time, Quebec committed up to $200 million in additional equity and Rio pledged more than $300 million for its Quebec lithium business during 2026. The province described its contribution as its final investment and said Rio had committed to bringing the plant into service in 2028. The latest reported pause would leave the construction restart uncertain in the very year previously targeted for first production. Lithium slump Lithium carbonate spot prices in Asia have fallen to $12.90 per kilogram from more than $25 in May, BMO said Thursday, citing Fastmarkets. Weak demand growth and expanding supply from Africa and China have weighed on the market, BMO said. Rio is also reviewing the plant’s long-term supply of spodumene, the lithium-bearing mineral used to make lithium hydroxide. The company has been assessing Nemaska’s Whabouchi project and its wholly owned Galaxy project to determine the best source. In February, Rio expected that supply review to be finished in the first half of the year. BMO said Thursday that the choice between the two projects remained unresolved. Rio shares dropped 1.51% Thursday morning to $83.72 in NYSE trading, valuing the company at about $136 billion. The stock has ranged between $68.70 and $112.58 in the past year.

title: Titan, US military team up on graphite
zh_title: 泰坦与美国军方合作开发石墨

content:
Titan Mining（纽约证券交易所股票代码：TII；多伦多证券交易所股票代码：TI）正致力于成为 70 年来美国第一家商业石墨生产商，同时寻求与陆军达成历史性协议，在阿拉巴马州基地建立石墨加工厂。根据拟议的交易，泰坦将把石墨精矿从其主要的基尔伯恩矿场和纽约州北部的示范工厂运送到安尼斯顿陆军仓库，泰坦的帝国矿业子公司将在那里利用一些现有的基础设施进一步加工石墨。该仓库位于阿拉巴马州首府蒙哥马利东北约145公里处。 Titan 首席执行官丽塔·阿迪亚尼 (Rita Adiani) 在 10 月份接受《北方矿工》采访时表示：“能够生产精矿真是太好了，但除非你能进一步精炼，否则你最终会面临同样的情况，即基本上将中游出口回中国或其他地方。” “这使我们能够有效地在国内生产端到端产品，从供应链安全的角度来看，这非常重要。”  政府与行业动力 6 月份，根据美国陆军战略资本计划 (SCI) 计划，该基地合作伙伴关系标志着政府、军方和工业界之间的重大合作，因为美国越来越多地寻求将关键矿产供应链置于国内控制之下并摆脱中国的影响。
在正在考虑的三个陆军基地中，包括纽约的德拉姆堡和阿肯色州的派恩布拉夫兵工厂，泰坦的安尼斯顿基地交易已进展为商业条款清单，尽管最终的租约尚未完成。安尼斯顿的租约涵盖最初的 50 年，以及两个额外的 25 年续约选项。根据 SCI 计划入选的其他公司包括 REalloys (纳斯达克股票代码：ALOY) 和 Ioneer (ASX: INR)，它们获得了有条件租赁合同，分别在犹他州 Tooele Army Depot 开发单独的重稀土和硼加工设施；私人公司 EnergyX 拥有德克萨斯州红河基地一座锂工厂的有条件租赁权。 13 年使用寿命 根据 2025 年起的初步经济评估 (PEA)，Kilbourne 在 13 年使用寿命内每年可按铭牌产能生产约 40,000 吨石墨精矿。Titan 于 1 月份开始在 Kilbourne 生产，并已向客户运送了至少 1,600 公斤石墨精矿。按 7% 折现，其税后净现值为 5.13 亿美元，税后内部收益率为 37%，初始成本为 1.56 亿美元。根据 2024 年的初步估计，PEA 基于 240 万吨品位为 2.91% 的石墨碳 (Cg) 推断，其中露天有限资源中含有 653,000 短吨石墨。综合采矿和加工业务的可行性研究正在进行中，预计将于 2027 年上半年发布。

【原文 English Original】
Titan Mining (NYSE-A: TII; TSX: TI) is working to become the first commercial graphite producer in the United States in 70 years while pursuing an historic agreement with the Army to set up a graphite processing plant on a base in Alabama.   The proposed deal would see Titan ship graphite concentrate from its main Kilbourne mine and demonstration plant in upstate New York to the Anniston Army Depot, where Titan’s Empire Mines subsidiary would further process the graphite using some existing infrastructure. The depot is about 145 km northeast of Alabama state capital Montgomery.   “It’s great to be able to produce a concentrate, but unless you can refine it down further, you end up facing that same situation where you’re basically exporting the midstream back to China or somewhere else,” Titan CEO Rita Adiani told The Northern Miner in an October interview.   “This allows us to effectively get to an end-to-end product domestically, which is pretty significant from a supply chain security standpoint.”  Government-industry momentum   Selected under the U.S. Army’s Strategic Capital Initiatives (SCI) program in June, the base partnership marks significant cooperation between the government, military and industry as the U.S. increasingly seeks to bring critical mineral supply chains under domestic control and outside the influence of China.   Of the three Army bases under consideration, including Fort Drum in New York and Pine Bluff Arsenal in Arkansas, Titan’s Anniston base deal has progressed to a commercial term sheet, although a definitive lease remains outstanding. The Anniston lease covers an initial 50 years with two additional 25-year renewal options.  The other companies selected under the SCI program include REalloys (Nasdaq: ALOY) and Ioneer (ASX: INR), which received conditional lease awards to develop separate heavy rare earth and boron processing facilities, respectively, at Tooele Army Depot in Utah; and private firm EnergyX, which has a conditional lease for a lithium plant at the Red River base in Texas.   13-year life   Kilbourne could produce about 40,000 tonnes of graphite concentrate annually at nameplate capacity over a 13-year life, according to a preliminary economic assessment (PEA) from 2025. Titan began production at Kilbourne in January and has shipped at least 1,600 kg of graphite concentrate to customers.   Discounted at 7%, it has a post-tax net present value of $513 million, a post-tax internal rate of return of 37% and initial costs of $156 million.  The PEA is based on 2.4 million inferred tons grading 2.91% graphitic carbon (Cg), containing 653,000 short tons of graphite in open-pit constrained resources, according to a 2024 initial estimate.   A feasibility study is under way for the integrated mining and processing operation, expected to be released in the first half of 2027.  Titan also produces zinc through Empire State Mines at Kilbourne, about 480 km northwest of New York City.  Army base advantages   While there are some industrial sites in the region around Kilbourne that could be compatible with Titan’s downstream processing vision, New York’s permitting timelines are relatively long, Adiani said. As well, permitting a downstream facility requires close access to a wastewater treatment plant, which the Anniston base has.   “[Its] wastewater treatment facility is effectively used for ammunition cleaning,” Adiani said. “That moves things forward from a permitting standpoint, and it makes it easy for us to plug and play into that infrastructure. It ends up saving us a lot of capex and operating costs.”  The timeline to production for the Kilbourne-Anniston supply chain starts with the feasibility study, followed by an investment decision and permits before the end of 2027, Adiani said. Construction would take about 15 months, with production starting in 2028 or 2029.   Fine processing at Anniston   Kilbourne’s graphite concentrate and micronized graphite concentrate would be shipped to Anniston for producing purified micronized graphite (PMG) and then coated spherical purified graphite (CSPG), highly purified graphite that is shaped into tiny particles and used in anodes for lithium batteries.   Initial production of PMG is pegged at 10,000 tons and could start around 2029, Adiani said. Titan is still determining if it would come from Kilbourne or Anniston. A few years later, CSPG output would start from Anniston, ramping up to 20,000 tons.   Kilbourne is also covered by the U.S. government’s FAST-41 permitting program, intended to improve coordination and transparency for major infrastructure projects.  Army’s 10% share   Under Titan’s agreement, the Army has a right of first offer to buy up to 10% of annual PMG and CSPG output. Other potential graphite customers include refractory supplier RHI Magnesita and an unnamed U.S. aerospace and defence manufacturer.   Titan could invest between $30 million and $70 million in the Anniston plant, Adiani said. The U.S. Export-Import Bank has separately proposed up to $120 million in construction financing for Kilbourne and agreed to provide $5.5 million for feasibility work.  Market catch-up   Despite the recent positive developments, Titan’s share price is about 30% over the past year. The stock traded at C$2.74 apiece in Toronto on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalization of C$271.3 million ($190 million). The stock has traded in a 12-month range of C$2.55 to C$7.75. “The key thing people should remember is that until two years ago Titan traded at 30 cents,” Adiani said. “That 654% increase in two years is not going to be sustained.”  Investors want to see how Titan is de-risking its operations by completing the Kilbourne feasibility study, organizing offtake deals and completing the financing with U.S. EXIM, Adiani suggests.  “There are some key catalysts due for later this year and early next year, which will provide that momentum and sustaining back to those levels.”

title: OpenAI launches security products, tells orgs they’re doomed if they don’t use them

content:
OpenAI 推出了两种新的安全产品，一种用于渗透测试，另一种用于防御，并警告组织只有使用此类工具，他们的业务才是安全的。 OpenAI 总裁格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 在周四的主题演讲中表示：“我们现在所处的阶段是，公司的安全取决于他们用来保护自己的前沿模型以及他们利用该模型的程度。”破坏安全性的公司的联合创始人确实承认，安全性“基础知识很重要，不容忽视”。然而，“你需要真正围绕这些模型的功能重新调整你的安全实践，”布罗克曼零讽刺地说道，并且大概谈论的是使用人工智能模型进行防御，而不是攻击其他组织。 “产品也很重要。”当然，这个产品应该来自 OpenAI，为此，该公司推出了 Daybreak Red Team 和 Daybreak Defense Factory，它们都是 OpenAI Daybreak 安全平台的一部分。 Red Team 现已推出抢先体验版，它使用 OpenAI 模型来测试公司的 Web 应用程序是否存在漏洞。网络应用人工智能的领导者 Nancy Wang 将其描述为“自动连续扫描规模的超人笔测试”，一组代理使用源代码和应用程​​序上下文来调查和测试攻击路径。
它还帮助安全团队验证报告的漏洞（来自代码扫描器、错误赏金计划和披露报告），然后测试这些缺陷的补丁。第二个产品 Daybreak Defense Factory 通过“大规模查找、验证和修复漏洞”来自动化“防御循环”。该模型还使用基于 OpenAI 最新网络模型构建的代理 - 目前为 GPT-6 Cyber​​ 。这些代理扫描组织的代码库，寻找漏洞并开发补丁。工程师在投入生产之前审查并批准建议的修复方案。 “通过这种方式，工程师可以获得带有补丁的合并就绪拉取请求，并进行测试以证明其有效，”王说。与此同时，正当 OpenAI 高管宣传新的安全产品时，一个非营利组织联盟向旧金山高等法院提起诉讼，要求法官阻止 OpenAI、Anthropic、谷歌、Meta 和 SpaceX 的人工智能业务开发或部署比其最先进的现有模型更强大的人工智能系统。该诉讼由 Irreplaceable Education Fund、Public Citizen、Heat Initiative 和 The Alliance for Secure AI 提起，列举了 OpenAI 代理访问 Hugging Face、未经授权访问包含医疗保险统计数据的澳大利亚政府门户网站以及其他与人工智能相关的网络安全事件的事件。
法庭文件称，“被告告诉我们，他们正在开发的人工智能技术给公众带来了灾难性风险，包括引发人工智能驱动的网络攻击和生物武器”，并补充说人工智能公司“并没有错”。 ®

【原文 English Original】
OpenAI has launched two new security products, one for penetration testing and another for defense, and warned organizations that their businesses are only safe if they use tools like these. “We're now at a point where companies will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves and how well they utilize that,” OpenAI President Greg Brockman said during a Thursday keynote address. The co-founder of the company that broke security did admit that security “fundamentals are important, and not to be discounted.” However, “you need to really reorient your security practice around what these models can do,” Brockman said, with zero irony, and presumably talking about using AI models for defense - not for hacking other organizations . “Also very important is product.” This product, of course, should come from OpenAI, and, to that end, the company rolled out Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory, which are both part of OpenAI’s Daybreak security platform. Red Team , which is available in early access, uses OpenAI models to test companies’ web applications for vulnerabilities. Nancy Wang, who leads cyber-applied AI, described it as “superhuman pen-test at the scale of automated continuous scanning,” with a fleet of agents using source code and app context to investigate and test attack paths. It also helps security teams validate reported vulnerabilities - from code scanners, bug bounty programs, and disclosure reports - and then test the patches for these flaws. The second product, Daybreak Defense Factory , automates the “defensive loop” by “finding, validating, and fixing vulnerabilities at scale.” This one also uses agents built on OpenAI’s latest cyber models - currently, that’s GPT-6 Cyber . The agents scan organizations’ codebases, hunting for vulnerabilities and developing patches. Engineers review and approve the proposed fixes before they go into production. “This way engineers get a merge-ready pull request with the patch and a test that shows that it works,” Wang said. Meanwhile, as OpenAI execs touted the new security products, a coalition of nonprofits filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court asking a judge to stop OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceX's AI businesses from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most advanced existing models. The lawsuit , filed by Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, and The Alliance for Secure AI, cites incidents involving OpenAI agents accessing Hugging Face , gaining unauthorized access to an Australian government portal containing Medicare statistics , and other AI-related cybersecurity incidents . “Defendants tell us that the AI technology they are developing poses catastrophic risks to the public, including by enabling AI-driven cyberattacks and bioweapons,” the court documents allege, adding that the AI companies “are not wrong.” ®

title: Jensen Huang's self-sabotage sends Nvidia into a midlife crisis
zh_title: 黄仁勋的自我破坏让英伟达陷入中年危机
summary: 英伟达首席执行官兼创始人黄仁勋在经历了近两周的争议后被赶下台，这些争议有时感觉更像是肥皂剧而不是现实：一个富商、报道的绯闻以及一名涉嫌中国间谍和 GPU 走私者。对于英伟达董事会来说，黄仁勋的离开似乎是毫无疑问的。事实证明，这位最近成为世界上最有价值公司的幕后黑手承担了太大的责任，无法以任何身份保留。即使从首席执行官降职为董事长，他也太有毒了，即使他不再被信任，这一有利地位仍能让黄作为公司的代言人。
content:
英伟达首席执行官兼创始人黄仁勋在经历了近两周的争议后被赶下台，这些争议有时感觉更像是肥皂剧而不是现实：一个富商、报道的绯闻以及一名涉嫌中国间谍和 GPU 走私者。对于英伟达董事会来说，黄仁勋的离开似乎是毫无疑问的。事实证明，这位最近成为世界上最有价值公司的幕后黑手承担了太大的责任，无法以任何身份保留。即使从首席执行官降职为董事长，他也太有毒了，即使不再信任他来管理公司，这一有利地位仍将使黄作为公司的代言人。取代他不会那么容易。英伟达现在面临着身份危机。黄先生领导该公司三十多年，目前还没有明确的继任者。 GPU 投手不乏才华横溢的工程师，但能够与世界上最大、最有影响力的品牌之一争吵的高管则不然。 CUDA 之父、Nvidia 超大规模和 HPC 副总裁伊恩·巴克 (Ian Buck) 目前被许多人视为黄仁勋的继任者。近年来，巴克在英伟达内部扮演了更加公开的角色，在超级计算和人工智能基础设施峰会等活动上发表主题演讲。首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 是一名精打细算的人，十多年来一直坚持詹森的雄心壮志，现在，在董事会寻找下一任傀儡领导人时，她现在担任临时首席执行官。
尽管克雷斯努力遏制混乱，但其他人无疑会利用黄氏有争议的配偶选择来推进自己的议程。 声誉受损 人们只需要问几个不方便的问题就可以对英伟达的忠诚度产生怀疑。中国对英伟达的影响力有多深？ Nvidia的硬件还可以信任吗？你明白了。这当然不是英伟达以及黄仁勋的忠诚第一次受到质疑。 2023 年末，Cerebras 首席执行官安德鲁·费尔德曼 (Andrew Feldman) 抨击竞争对手英伟达不顾美国出口管制向中国供应 GPU，称这种行为“不美国”，并将这家图形巨头比作人工智能军火商。英伟达还面临美国政府官员的批评，其中包括前商务部长吉娜·雷蒙多(Gina Raimondo)，称其没有接受暗示，而是试图在美国出口管制下陷入困境，以继续向中国出售芯片。去年年初，特朗普政府短暂封锁 H20 销售，使该公司损失了约 105 亿美元，此后，黄仁勋在 2025 年的大部分时间里游说特朗普政府撤销对中国销售老一代 Hopper 一代 GPU 的出口禁令，这一努力最终证明是成功的。有人可能会认为，黄仁勋不断向中国出售英伟达芯片的努力是出于经济动机。
但黄承认与 Megaspeed 执行官 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）有婚外情，这一论点被削弱了。美国情报部门指控她兼职担任中国间谍，并帮助将 GPU 走私到中国。 争议的后果 当技术和政治发生冲突时，不当行为的表象往往比不当行为本身更可怕。山姆大叔迫使中国公司撤离美国，仅仅是因为它们可能被迫在关键基础设施中安装后门。只要问问华为，一旦华盛顿认定你对国家安全构成威胁，真相是否还重要。黄的事件可能不仅让他失去工作，还可能让英伟达失去关键

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang has been ousted after nearly two weeks of controversy that, at times, felt more like a soap opera than reality: a wealthy businessman, reported affairs, and an alleged Chinese spy and GPU smuggler. For Nvidia’s board, it seems there was no question Huang had to go. The man behind what was recently the most valuable company in the world proved too big a liability to retain in any capacity. He was too toxic even for a demotion from CEO to chairman, a vantage point that would have retained Huang as the face of the company even if he could no longer be trusted to run it. Replacing him won’t be so easy. Nvidia now faces an identity crisis. Huang, who has led the company for more than three decades, has no clear successor. The GPU slinger has no shortage of brilliant engineers, but executives capable of wrangling one of the biggest and most influential brands in the world, not so much. Ian Buck, father of CUDA and Nvidia’s VP of hyperscale and HPC is currently favored by many to be Huang’s successor. Buck has taken on a more public role within Nvidia in recent years headlining keynotes at events like Supercomputing and the AI Infra Summit. CFO Colette Kress, a bean counter who’s kept Jensen’s ambitions grounded for more than a decade, now takes the reins as interim CEO while the board searches for its next figurehead. And while Kress fights to contain the chaos, others will no doubt capitalize on Huang’s controversial choice of consorts to advance their own agendas. A marred reputation One need only ask a few inconvenient questions to cast doubt on Nvidia’s loyalties. How deep does China’s influence in Nvidia go? Can Nvidia’s hardware still be trusted? You get the idea. It certainly wouldn’t be the first time Nvidia’s and, by extension, Huang’s loyalties have been called into question. In late 2023, Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman blasted rival Nvidia for supplying GPUs to China in spite of US export controls, calling the behavior “ un-American ” and likening the graphics titan to an AI arms dealer. Nvidia has also faced criticism from US government officials, including former commerce secretary Gina Raimondo, for failing to take a hint and trying instead to limbo under US export controls in order to continue selling chips to the Middle Kingdom. After the Trump administration's short lived blockade of H20 sales early last year cost the company some $10.5 billion, Huang spent much of the 2025 lobbying the Trump administration to reverse export bans on the sales of older Hopper generation GPUs to China, an endeavor which ultimately proved successful . One could make the case that Huang’s ongoing efforts to sell Nvidia’s chips to China were financially motivated. But that argument is undermined by Huang admitting to having an extramarital affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang (no relation), a woman that US intelligence has accused of moonlighting as a Chinese spy and helping to smuggle GPUs into the country. The consequences of controversy When technology and politics collide, the appearance of impropriety is often more damning than the impropriety itself. Uncle Sam has forced Chinese companies out of the United States for the mere possibility that they could be coerced into planting back doors in critical infrastructure. Just ask Huawei whether the truth counts for anything once Washington has decided that you’re a national security threat. Huang’s affairs may not just cost him his job, but could cost Nvidia key government contracts and make the company’s hardware less attractive, particularly in highly-regulated and notoriously risk-averse industries. Rival chipmakers will no doubt capitalize on Nvidia’s bad optics if Huang’s departure doesn’t pop the AI financing merry-go-round bubble first – Nvidia's stock lost about 25% of its value in the few days after news about Huang started breaking, only recovering slightly after his ouster. Regardless, with Nvidia’s reputation marred and its future shrouded in uncertainty, once loyal customers may be more willing to explore alternative providers. There are certainly plenty to choose from. Amid a surge in custom AI chips from the likes of Broadcom, Marvel, and others, Nvidia’s main advantage wasn’t so much technological as it was simply considered a safe bet. AMD is the most obvious winner here. As we reported earlier this year , the House of Zen’s GPU tech has already surpassed Nvidia’s, at least on paper. What’s more, the company has a long and unblemished relationship serving the US government. AMD’s chips now power two of the Department of Energy’s three largest and most sensitive supercomputers. Meanwhile, hyperscalers with sufficient cashflow – think Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta – may seek to insulate themselves from Huang’s fallout by investing more heavily in homegrown silicon and offering it to customers. Then there's the threat from the man himself. Huang's ambitions and influence are such that he's unlikely to fade into obscurity. He may disappear from the spotlight while things blow over, but it’s a pretty sure bet that he’ll pop up at a new company eventually, and will still have enough sway to poach some of Nvidia’s top engineers. ®

title: How the effects of Jensen Huang’s ouster are spiraling out through the economy
zh_title: 黄仁勋下台的影响如何在经济中蔓延

content:
英伟达和黄仁勋并不是唯一受到关注的公司。这位长期担任科技高管的一周经历了糟糕的一周。这一切都始于黄与一名被指控为中国政府的间谍有婚外情的消息浮出水面。作为回应，黄仁勋 30 多年前共同创立的 Nvidia 公司董事会开始了调查。美国联邦调查局（FBI）也展开调查。周三有消息称，黄至少还发生过另一桩婚外情，这次是与一名直接向他汇报的公司高管发生了婚外情。到周四早上，黄仁勋已经辞职，芯片公司任命了一位临时首席执行官。但热门歌曲不断涌现。周四下午，路透社报道称，黄与另一名员工发生了婚外情。显然，这对于英伟达来说是个坏消息。股市下跌，现在准备夺回国会的民主党人似乎正在加紧调查该公司以及美国国家安全可能面临的任何风险的计划。但这对于与英伟达的成功息息相关的一系列其他实体来说也是不利的。以下是一些感受到一些反弹的因素。白宫 刚刚在中期选举中遭受惨重损失的白宫将面临质疑，为什么它在得知黄与一名涉嫌间谍的恋情后推迟采取行动。
特朗普政府在安全和情报实践方面的声誉本来就很差，但似乎对这些知识的忽视几乎肯定会增加进一步调查的可能性。值得注意的是，特朗普官员已经批准了允许英伟达向中国出售先进计算机芯片的协议，甚至在地缘政治谈判中利用美国对该公司芯片的影响力。 NVIDIA 现有和潜在客户美国人工智能供应链在 Nvidia 上运行。 OpenAI、Anthropic 和许多其他大型语言模型开发人员都依赖该公司的硬件。 Meta、微软和甲骨文也是主要客户。这在很大程度上是因为 GPU（或图形处理单元）特别擅长开发大型推理模型所需的计算。现在，由于对英伟达的审查如此之多，这些公司以及任何正在进行的交易都可能面临阻力，因为仍在混乱的董事会正在考虑下一步该做什么。支持芯片公司的主要贸易组织半导体行业协会拒绝发表评论。今年早些时候同意被英伟达收购的人工智能开发商 Hugging Face 没有回应置评请求。值得注意的是，黄似乎没有继任计划。 Nvidia 首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 于周四上午被任命为临时首席执行官。丑闻和混乱不仅对需要英伟达芯片的美国公司不利。
考虑到黄仁勋主张放宽对中国芯片销售限制的程度，任何涉嫌与中国政府有联系的客户也可能会看到英伟达交易受到比以前更严格的审查。联邦机构美国政府是英伟达的主要支持者，在自己的系统（包括机密网络）中广泛使用该公司的技术。本周的爆料不仅让政府感到尴尬，而且引发了人们的担忧：政府官员对黄与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情的了解程度，以及他们可能如何影响该公司与联邦机构的往来。一位前联邦首席信息官告诉《快公司》

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia and Jensen Huang aren’t the only ones in the crosshairs.  The longtime tech executive has had a bad week. It all began when news surfaced that Huang had been having an extramarital affair with an alleged spy for the Chinese government. In response, the corporate board of Nvidia—the company Huang cofounded more than 30 years ago—began an investigation. The FBI launched a probe, too. Then news broke Wednesday that Huang had engaged in at least one other affair, this time with a company executive who reported directly to him. By Thursday morning, Huang had resigned , and the chip company had appointed an interim CEO. But the hits kept coming. Thursday afternoon Reuters reported that Huang had engaged in an affair with a second employee . Obviously, this is bad news for Nvidia. Stocks are down, and Democrats, now preparing to take back Congress, appear to be ramping up plans to investigate the company and any possible risks to U.S. national security. But this is also bad for a range of other entities that have a stake in Nvidia’s success. Here are a few that stand to feel some of the blowback. The White House The White House, fresh off of devastating losses in the midterm elections, stands to face questions about why it held off on taking action after it learned about Huang’s affair with an alleged spy. The Trump administration already had a poor reputation for security and intelligence practices, but seemingly sleeping on this knowledge is all but certain to raise the prospect of further probes. Trump officials, notably, have cleared deals allowing Nvidia to sell advanced computer chips to China, and even leveraged U.S. influence over the company’s chips in geopolitical negotiations. Current and prospective NVIDIA customers The U.S. AI supply chain runs on Nvidia. OpenAI, Anthropic, and a slew of other large language model developers rely on the company’s hardware. Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle are also major customers. This is, in large part, because GPUs—or graphics processing units—are particularly adept at the kinds of computations needed to develop large reasoning models.  Now, with so much scrutiny on Nvidia, there’s a risk those companies—and any deals in progress—might face headwinds as the still-scrambling board figures out what to do next. The Semiconductor Industry Association, a major trade group that advocates for chip companies, declined to comment. Hugging Face, an AI developer that agreed to an acquisition by Nvidia earlier this year, did not respond to a request for comment.  Remarkably, Huang doesn’t seem to have had a succession plan. Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, was appointed interim CEO on Thursday morning. The scandal and disarray isn’t just bad for American companies that need Nvidia’s chips. Given the extent to which Huang advocated for loosening chip sale limits to China, any customers with suspected links to the Chinese government may also see far more scrutiny on Nvidia deals than before. U.S. federal agencies The U.S. government is a major supporter of Nvidia, using the company’s tech extensively in its own systems, including classified networks . The revelations this week are not only embarrassing for the government, but raise concerns about the extent to which government officials were aware of Huang’s affair with a suspected spy for China, and how they might have influenced the company’s dealings with federal agencies. One former federal chief information officer told Fast Company that the scandal raises suspicions that the U.S. security clearance system, which is supposed to engage in continuous monitoring, isn’t as up to snuff as it should be. Everyone else  We really are that dependent on Nvidia. If we learned anything from the chip shortage we experienced during the pandemic, the semiconductor market is heavily concentrated, and disruptions with just one company can quickly ripple through the economy. In 2020, it was companies like TSMC, a Taiwan-based contract manufacturer that supplies chips for a host of devices. And the stock market—including pension funds and 401(k) plans—are deeply exposed to Nvidia stock. “It is striking that Nvidia, a $4 trillion company central to both the AI economy and U.S. equity markets, appears to have no publicly identified successor to Jensen Huang,” Ann Lewis, a technology executive and former U.S. government tech official, told Fast Company Wednesday. “In cybersecurity, we call this a single point of failure. A company of this scale should not depend so completely on one person’s relationships and judgment.”

title: Jensen Huang brought a lot more to Nvidia than a cult of personality. Why his downfall hits so hard
zh_title: 黄仁勋给英伟达带来的不仅仅是个人崇拜。为什么他的垮台如此严重
summary: 现在，你可能已经听说过：英伟达联合创始人黄仁勋周四在证实有外遇后辞职。处于这一切中心的女性艾丽丝·黄（无亲属关系）被指控为中国间谍，这听起来像是从詹姆斯·邦德惊悚片中撕下来的一页。现在有报道称，黄还至少与英伟达员工发生过两起婚外情。这起丑闻充满了阴谋和真实的后果，包括国家安全担忧以及英伟达股价持续下跌对金融市场的重大打击。 Nvidia Corp.（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）做到了
content:
现在，你可能已经听说过：英伟达联合创始人黄仁勋周四在证实有外遇后辞职。处于这一切中心的女性艾丽丝·黄（无亲属关系）被指控为中国间谍，这听起来像是从詹姆斯·邦德惊悚片中撕下来的一页。现在有报道称，黄还至少与英伟达员工发生过两起婚外情。这起丑闻充满了阴谋和真实的后果，包括国家安全担忧以及英伟达股价持续下跌对金融市场的重大打击。截至撰写本文时，英伟达公司（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）在周四下午交易中下跌约 5%，自丑闻爆发以来，该公司在过去几天遭受了两位数的损失。总而言之，这些事态发展凸显了黄仁勋独特的地缘政治价值，因为他和他的人工智能芯片处于美国与中国人工智能军备竞赛的中心。据《纽约时报》报道，Nvidia 控制着约 90% 的用于人工智能的先进芯片市场。他的离开对英伟达来说是一个巨大的损失，这超出了他巨大的个性的范围，这使他成为科技行业最大的媒体宠儿之一。这也超出了他与唐纳德·特朗普总统关系密切的范围，后者本周早些时候为黄的“出色工作”辩护并称赞。有报道称，特朗普知道黄的外遇。
据《华盛顿邮报》报道，特朗普于 5 月 12 日在空军一号上听取了国务卿马可·卢比奥的情况通报，《纽约时报》则报道称，特朗普早在 2025 年 10 月就获悉黄仁勋和黄爱丽丝的“亲密关系”。特朗普方面则否认在 5 月份听说过此事。 “可悲的是，伟大并不保证善良。这令人失望，”风险投资家莎拉·郭在 X 上写道。“《经济学人》说‘没有人是不可替代的’。他们错了。”黄仁勋的价值不仅来自于他创立并共同创立了英伟达（并且仍然是该公司最大的个人股东），还来自于他在亚洲的密切个人和商业关系。他与台积电创始人张忠谋等关键人物的关系为英伟达确保了庞大的供应链渠道。另一个问题是：黄仁勋离开英伟达正值关键的政治时刻，紧随民主党在上周的中期选举中所谓的“蓝色海啸”席卷国会之后，硅谷迎来了一个新时代，并可能突然结束其与华盛顿共和党的亲密关系。参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 在 X 周四发帖称：“国会必须要求黄先生和 Nvidia 的其他人就他们可能如何将美国国家安全置于危险之中提供答案。” “特朗普政府还必须对得知特朗普的所作所为负责。
黄先生与一名疑似中国情报人员的关系。政府官员是否因为特朗普与黄先生的关系而被告知不要调查？特朗普亲自邀请黄先生登上空军一号时，他知道什么？”

【原文 English Original】
By now, you have probably heard: Nvidia’s cofounder Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he confirmed having an affair . The woman at the center of it all, Alice Huang (no relation), is alleged to be a Chinese spy , in a twist that sounds like a page ripped from a James Bond thriller. Reports now suggest that Huang also had at least two other affairs with employees at Nvidia. The scandal is rife with intrigue and all-too-real consequences—including national security concerns and a major hit to the financial markets, as Nvidia’s share price continues to fall. Nvidia Corp. (Nasdaq: NVDA ) was down about 5% in afternoon trading on Thursday at the time of this writing, after suffering double-digit losses over the past few days since the scandal broke. Altogether, the developments shine a spotlight on Huang’s unique geopolitical value, as he—and his AI chips—sit at the center of the U.S. AI arms race with China. Nvidia controls about 90% of the advanced chips market used for AI, per The New York Times . His departure is a big loss for Nvidia—one that goes beyond his outsize personality, which made him one of the tech industry’s biggest media darlings. It also goes beyond his close proximity to President Donald Trump , who earlier this week defended and praised Huang for doing a “fantastic job.” Reports allege that Trump knew about Huang’s affair. According to The Washington Post , Trump was briefed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the situation on May 12 on Air Force One, and The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed about Jensen Huang’s and Alice Huang’s “close relationship” as early as October 2025. Trump, for his part, denied hearing about the situation in May. “Sadly, greatness doesn’t guarantee goodness. It’s disappointing,” venture capitalist Sarah Guo wrote on X. “ The Economist says ‘no one is irreplaceable.’ They are very wrong.” Huang’s value comes not only from the fact that he built and co-founded Nvidia—and remains the company’s largest individual shareholder —but also from his close personal and business connections in Asia . His relationships with key figures like TSMC founder Morris Chang have secured a massive supply chain pipeline for Nvidia. Another issue: Huang’s departure from Nvidia comes at a critical political moment, on the heels of the Democratic Party’s so-called “blue tsunami” sweep into Congress in last week’s midterm elections, ushering in a new era for Silicon Valley—and likely bringing an abrupt end to its cozy relationship with Washington’s Republicans. “Congress must demand answers from Mr. Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put U.S. national security at risk,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer posted on X Thursday. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?”

title: Jensen Huang Is Out. The Misogyny Is Forever.
zh_title: 黄仁勋出局了。厌女症是永远的。
summary: 由于丑闻不断扩大和股价暴跌，黄仁勋辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。人工智能领域最著名的人物之一被驱逐之前，黄承认了与一名被美国政府认定为中国政府可能间谍的女性的婚外情，以及随后的一份谴责性报道称他与一名直接下属发生了外遇。然而，在股价暴跌的情况下，黄与世界上一些最有权势的人所享有的一致支持几乎肯定会保持不变。 “那将是一种荣幸，”埃隆·马斯克写道
content:
由于丑闻不断扩大和股价暴跌，黄仁勋辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。人工智能领域最著名的人物之一被驱逐之前，黄承认了与一名被美国政府认定为中国政府可能间谍的女性的婚外情，以及随后的一份谴责性报道称他与一名直接下属发生了外遇。然而，在股价暴跌的情况下，黄与世界上一些最有权势的人所享有的一致支持几乎肯定会保持不变。 “那将是一种荣幸，”埃隆·马斯克周三写道，在第二起婚外情的消息传出后，一名网络影响者请求这位亿万富翁雇用黄。比尔·阿克曼等人呼吁公众支持这位陷入困境的皮夹克爱好者和“不可思议的人”。尚未对黄的辞职发表评论的美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一称他为“高素质的人”，并驳斥了有关他与国务卿马可·卢比奥和多名美国国家安全官员了解黄与涉嫌中国间谍的关系的报道。这种腐烂的情况远远超出了它可能反映有权势人物的私人思想的范围。他们共同明确了对一项经常复制他们自己的性别歧视和性别偏见的技术的支持。在网上，一致的支持明显转向了厌恶女性。
数百名评论者（其中许多是假的）发布了照片，尖刻地将黄仁勋结婚四十多年的妻子 Lori Huang 与据称与黄仁勋有外遇的 Alice Huang 进行比较。全文的潜台词很明确：黄仁勋的长期伴侣不再具有足够的吸引力；他的妻子不再有足够的吸引力；他的妻子不再那么有吸引力。事情是有道理的。正如一位用户写道：“我不容忍出轨，但黄仁勋的情况提醒我们，女性也需要看起来最漂亮。他的妻子看起来简直就像他的奶奶一样。” “男人应该赚钱、保持光彩、永远看起来很好。女人一旦拿到戒指就不能停止尝试，否则你会迫使男人升级！”这些评论似乎说出了像特朗普这样的人不能说的话，至少不能公开地说。但这种腐败现象远远超出了权力人物私人思想的可能反映。他们共同明确了对一项经常复制他们自己的性别歧视和性别偏见的技术的支持。事实上，像马斯克和特朗普这样的男人自己也曾说过同样的厌女症的不同版本。 “看看那张脸！会有人投票吗？你能想象那是我们下一任总统的脸吗？！”特朗普曾这样评价卡莉·菲奥莉娜。考虑到大量研究表明，大型语言模型充斥着厌女症，经常将女性视为性对象和男性的财产——马斯克在 X 上放大了这一想法。这项技术主要由男性主导、由男性设计，并且更有可能由男性使用。
既然他们自己的一个人陷入了性丑闻——这一丑闻对国家安全产生了深远的影响——那么支持就自然而然了。总统和马斯克尚未在自己的社交媒体账户上分享这些卑鄙的帖子之一，这可能表明了某种克制。但他们对黄仁勋的支持可能会越来越大，黄仁勋现在在他们眼中可能是烈士。

【原文 English Original】
Amid an ever-expanding scandal and plunging shares, Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO. The ouster of one of the most prominent figures in artificial intelligence comes after Huang admitted to an extramarital affair involving a woman the US government has identified as a possible spy for the Chinese government, as well as a subsequent damning report that he had carried out an affair with a direct report. Yet, amid tanking stock prices, the lockstep support Huang enjoys with some of the world’s most powerful men is all but certain to remain intact. “That would be an honor,” Elon Musk wrote on Wednesday, responding to an online influencer’s plea for the trillionaire to hire Huang as news of the second affair emerged. Others like Bill Ackman called on the public to back the embattled leather-jacket enthusiast and “incredible human.” President Donald Trump, who has yet to comment on Huang’s resignation, on Monday called him a “high-quality guy,” brushing off reports that he, along with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and multiple US national security officials, knew about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese spy. The rot goes far further than its likely reflection of the private thoughts of powerful men. Together, they crystallized the support for a technology that regularly replicates their own sexism and gender bias. Online, the chorus of support took a distinctly misogynistic turn. Hundreds of commenters— many of them fake —posted photos snarkily comparing Huang’s wife of over four decades, Lori Huang, to Alice Huang, with whom he allegedly had an affair. The subtext throughout was clear: Jensen Huang’s longtime partner was no longer sufficiently attractive; affairs were justified. As one user wrote: “I don’t condone cheating, but the Jensen Huang situation is a reminder that women need to looksmax too. His wife literally looks like she could be his grandma.” “Men are expected to make money, stay jacked, and look good forever. Women can’t just stop trying once they get the ring or you will force the man to upgrade!” It’s as if the comments were saying what men like Trump could not, at least not publicly. But the rot goes far beyond its likely reflection of the private thoughts of powerful men. Together, they crystallized the support for a technology that regularly replicates their own sexism and gender bias. In fact, men like Musk and Trump have themselves uttered variations of the same misogyny. “Look at that face! Would anyone vote for that? Can you imagine that, the face of our next president?!” Trump once said of Carly Fiorina. Consider that numerous studies have shown that large language models are rife with misogyny, often treating women as sex objects and the property of men— ideas Musk has amplified on X . This technology is primarily led by men, designed by men, and is far more likely to be used by men . Now that one of their own has been caught in a sex scandal—one with deep national security implications—the support comes naturally. That the president and Musk have yet to share one of these vile posts on their own social media accounts may be indicative of some kind of restraint. But their support for Jensen Huang, now a likely martyr in their eyes, may well grow louder.
